chapters: And these are the names of the sons of Yisroel who came to Mitzrayim with Yackov, each man and his household came.
Reuven, Shimon, Levi, and Yehudah;
Yissachar, Zevulun, and Binyamin;
Dan and Naftali, Gad and Asher.
And all the souls that came out of the loins of Yackov were seventy souls, and Yosef was in Mitzrayim.
And Yosef died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
And the sons of Yisroel were fruitful and swarmed and multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty, and the land was filled with them.
And a new king arose over Mitzrayim, who did not know Yosef.
And he said to his people: Behold, the people of the sons of Yisroel are more numerous and mightier than we.
Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it shall be, when war befalls us, that they too will join our enemies and fight against us and go up from the land.
And they set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens, and they built store cities for Paroh, Pitom and Rameses.
And as they afflicted them, so they multiplied and so they spread out, and they were disgusted because of the sons of Yisroel.
And the Mitzrim enslaved the sons of Yisroel with harshness.
And they embittered their lives with hard work, with mortar and with bricks, and with all work in the field, with all their work which they worked them with harshness.
And the king of Mitzrayim said to the Hebrew midwives, the name of the one was Shifra, and the name of the second was Puah.
And he said: When you deliver the Hebrew women, and you see them upon the birthstools, if it is a son, you shall kill him, and if it is a daughter, she shall live.
And the midwives feared Elokim, and they did not do as the king of Mitzrayim spoke to them, and they kept the children alive.
And the king of Mitzrayim called the midwives, and he said to them: Why did you do this thing, and you kept the children alive?
And the midwives said to Paroh: Because the Hebrew women are not like the Mitzri women, for they are vigorous, before the midwife comes to them they have given birth.
And Elokim did good to the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew very mighty.
And it was, because the midwives feared Elokim, He made for them houses.
And Paroh commanded all his people, saying: Every son that is born, into the river you shall cast him, and every daughter you shall keep alive.
And a man from the house of Levi went, and he took a daughter of Levi.
And the woman conceived and bore a son, and she saw him that he was good, and she hid him three months.

And she could no longer hide him, and she took for him a reed basket, and she coated it with clay and with pitch, and she placed the child in it, and she placed it in the reeds on the bank of the river.
And his sister stationed herself from afar, to know what would be done to him.
And the daughter of Paroh went down to bathe in the river, and her maidens were walking along the river, and she saw the basket among the reeds, and she sent her maidservant and she took it.
And she opened it and saw the child, and behold, a boy crying, and she had compassion on him, and she said: This is from the children of the Hebrews.
And his sister said to the daughter of Paroh: Shall I go and call for you a wet nurse from the Hebrew women, and she will nurse the child for you?
And the daughter of Paroh said to her: Go. And the girl went and called the mother of the child.
And the daughter of Paroh said to her: Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages. And the woman took the child and nursed him.
And the child grew, and she brought him to the daughter of Paroh, and he was a son to her, and she called his name Moshe, and she said: Because from the water I drew him.
And it was in those days, and Moshe grew, and he went out to his brethren and saw their burdens, and he saw a Mitzri man striking a Hebrew man from his brethren.
And he turned this way and that, and he saw that there was no man, and he struck the Mitzri and hid him in the sand.
And he went out on the second day, and behold, two Hebrew men fighting, and he said to the wicked one: Why do you strike your neighbor?
And he said: Who set you as a leader and a judge over us? Do you mean to kill me, as you killed the Mitzri? And Moshe feared, and he said: Indeed, the matter is known.
And Paroh heard this matter, and he sought to kill Moshe, and Moshe fled from before Paroh, and he settled in the land of Midyan, and he sat beside the well.
And the priest of Midyan had seven daughters, and they came and drew water and filled the troughs to give their father's flock to drink.
And the shepherds came and drove them away, and Moshe arose and saved them and gave their flock to drink.
And they came to Reuel their father, and he said: Why have you hurried to come today?
And they said: A Mitzri man rescued us from the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water for us and gave the flock to drink.
And he said to his daughters: And where is he? Why did you leave the man? Call him, and let him eat bread.
And Moshe agreed to dwell with the man, and he gave Tziporah his daughter to Moshe.
And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom, for he said: A stranger I was in a foreign land.
And it was in those many days, and the king of Mitzrayim died, and the sons of Yisroel sighed from the work, and they cried out, and their plea went up to Elokim from the work.
And Elokim heard their groaning, and Elokim remembered His covenant with Avraham, with Yitzchak, and with Yackov.
And Elokim saw the sons of Yisroel, and Elokim knew.
And Moshe was shepherding the flock of Yisro, his father-in-law, priest of Midyan, and he led the flock to the far side of the wilderness, and he came to the mountain of Elokim, to Chorev.
And a messenger of the Master appeared to him in a flame of fire from within the bush, and he saw, and behold, the bush was burning in the fire, and the bush was not consumed.
And Moshe said: Let me turn aside now, and I will see this great sight, why the bush does not burn.
And Havayah saw that he turned aside to see, and Elokim called him from within the bush, and He said: Moshe, Moshe. And he said: Here I am.
And He said: Do not draw near here, remove your shoes from your feet, for the place upon which you are standing is sacred ground.
And He said: I am the Elokim of your father, the Elokim of Avraham, the Elokim of Yitzchak, and the Elokim of Yackov. And Moshe hid his face, for he feared to look upon Elokim.
And the Master said: I have surely seen the affliction of My people that is in Mitzrayim, and I have heard their outcry because of its taskmasters, for I know its pain.

And I have come down to rescue them from the hand of Mitzrayim, and to bring them up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Kena'anim and the Chitim and the Emorim and the Perizim and the Chivim and the Yevusim.
And now, behold, the outcry of the sons of Yisroel has come to Me, and I have also seen the oppression that the Mitzrim are oppressing them.
And now, go, and I will send you to Paroh, and bring out My people, the sons of Yisroel, from Mitzrayim.
And Moshe said to Elokim: Who am I, that I should go to Paroh, and that I should bring out the sons of Yisroel from Mitzrayim?
And He said: Because I will be with you, and this is your sign that I sent you: When you bring the people out of Mitzrayim, you will serve Elokim upon this mountain.

And Moshe said to Elokim: Behold, I come to the sons of Yisroel, and I will say to them: The Elokim of your fathers sent me to you, and they will say to me: What is His name? What shall I say to them?
And Elokim said to Moshe: I Will Be As I Will Be. And He said: So shall you say to the sons of Yisroel: I Will Be sent me to you.

And Elokim said further to Moshe: So shall you say to the sons of Yisroel: Havayah, Elokim of your fathers, Elokim of Avraham, Elokim of Yitzchak, and Elokim of Yackov, sent me to you. This is My name forever, and this is My remembrance for all generations.

Go and gather the elders of Yisroel, and say to them: Havayah, Elokim of your forefathers, Elokim of Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yackov, appeared to me, saying: I have surely remembered you, and what is done to you in Mitzrayim.

And I said: I will bring you up from the affliction of Mitzrayim to the land of the Kena'anim and the Chitim and the Emorim and the Perizim and the Chivim and the Yevusim, to a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they will listen to your voice, and you shall go, you and the elders of Yisroel, to the king of Mitzrayim, and you shall say to him: Havayah, Elokim of the Hebrews, has met with us, and now, please, let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to Havayah our Elokim.
And I know that the king of Mitzrayim will not let you go, except by a strong hand.
And I will stretch out My hand, and I will strike Mitzrayim with all My wonders that I will do in its midst, and afterward he will send you.
And I will give this people favor in the eyes of Mitzrayim, and it shall be, when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

And every woman shall ask from her neighbor and from the one lodging in her house silver vessels and gold vessels and garments, and you shall place them upon your sons and upon your daughters, and you shall despoil the Mitzrim.
And Moshe answered and said: But behold, they will not believe me, and they will not listen to my voice, for they will say: Havayah did not appear to you.
And the Master said to him: What is this in your hand? And he said: A staff.
And He said: Cast it to the ground. And he cast it to the ground, and it became a serpent, and Moshe fled from before it.
And the Master said to Moshe: Stretch out your hand and grasp its tail. And he stretched out his hand and seized it, and it became a staff in his hand.
So that they will believe that Havayah, Elokim of their fathers, Elokim of Avraham, Elokim of Yitzchak, and Elokim of Yackov, appeared to you.
And the Master said to him further: Bring your hand into your bosom. And he brought his hand into his bosom, and he took it out, and behold, his hand was leprous like snow.
And He said: Return your hand to your bosom. And he returned his hand to his bosom, and he took it out of his bosom, and behold, it was restored like his flesh.
And it shall be, if they do not believe you and do not listen to the voice of the first sign, they will believe the voice of the latter sign.

And it shall be, if they do not believe even these two signs, and they do not listen to your voice, you shall take from the water of the Ye'or and pour it on the dry land, and the water that you take from the Ye'or will become blood on the dry land.

And Moshe said to the Master: Please, my Master, I am not a man of words, neither from yesterday nor from the day before, nor since You have spoken to Your servant, for I am slow of speech and slow of tongue.
And the Master said to him: Who gives a mouth to man, or who makes mute or deaf, or seeing or blind? Is it not I, Havayah?
And now, go, and I will be with your mouth, and I will teach you what you shall say.
And he said: Please, my Master, send by the hand of him whom You will send.

And the anger of Havayah burned against Moshe, and He said: Is not Aharon the Levi your brother? I know that he can speak, and also, behold, he is coming out to meet you, and he will see you and rejoice in his heart.
And you shall speak to him, and you shall place the words in his mouth, and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you what you shall do.
And he shall speak for you to the people, and he shall be a mouth for you, and you shall be a leader for him.
And this staff you shall take in your hand, with which you shall perform the signs.

And Moshe went and returned to Yeter his father-in-law, and he said to him: Let me go now and return to my brethren who are in Mitzrayim, and see whether they are still alive. And Yisro said to Moshe: Go in peace.
And Havayah said to Moshe in Midyan: Go, return to Mitzrayim, for all the men who sought your life have died.
And Moshe took his wife and his sons, and he set them on the donkey, and he returned to the land of Mitzrayim, and Moshe took the staff of Elokim in his hand.

And Havayah said to Moshe: When you go to return to Mitzrayim, see all the wonders that I have placed in your hand, and perform them before Paroh, and I will harden his heart, and he will not send the people.
And you shall say to Paroh: So Havayah says: My firstborn son is Yisroel.
And I say to you: Send forth My son, and he will serve Me, and if you refuse to send him forth, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.
And it was on the way, in the lodging, and a messenger of Havayah encountered him and sought to kill him.
And Tziporah took a flint, and she cut the foreskin of her son, and she touched it to his feet, and she said: For a bridegroom of blood you are to me.
And he released him. Then she said: A bridegroom of blood, because of the circumcision.
And Havayah said to Aharon: Go to meet Moshe in the wilderness. And he went and met him at the mountain of Elokim, and he kissed him.
And Moshe told Aharon all the words of Havayah who sent him, and all the signs that He commanded him.
And Moshe and Aharon went, and they gathered all the elders of the sons of Yisroel.
And Aharon spoke all the words that Havayah spoke to Moshe, and he performed the signs before the eyes of the people.
And the people believed, and they heard that Havayah remembered the sons of Yisroel and that He saw their affliction, and they bowed and prostrated themselves.
And afterward Moshe and Aharon came, and they said to Paroh: So Havayah says, Elokim of Yisroel: Send forth My people, and they will celebrate for Me in the wilderness.
And Paroh said: Who is Havayah, that I should listen to His voice to send forth Yisroel? I do not know Havayah, and I also will not send forth Yisroel.

And they said: The Elokim of the Hebrews has met with us, please, let us go a journey of three days in the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to Havayah our Elokim, lest He strike us with pestilence or with the sword.
And the king of Mitzrayim said to them: Why, Moshe and Aharon, do you disturb the people from their work? Go to your burdens.
And Paroh said: Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you would make them cease from their burdens.
And Paroh commanded on that day the taskmasters of the people and their foremen, saying:
You shall not continue to give straw to the people to make bricks, as before. They shall go and gather straw for themselves.

And the count of the bricks that they made before, you shall impose upon them, you shall not diminish from it, for they are lazy, therefore they cry out, saying: Let us go and sacrifice to our Elokim.
Let the work be heavy upon the men, and they shall engage in it, and they shall not pay attention to false words.
And the taskmasters of the people and their foremen went out, and they said to the people, saying: So says Paroh: I am not giving you straw.
You, go take straw for yourselves from wherever you find it, for nothing will be diminished from your work.
And the people scattered in all the land of Mitzrayim to gather stubble for straw.
And the taskmasters pressed, saying: Finish your work, each day's portion on its day, as when there was straw.
And the foremen of the sons of Yisroel, whom Paroh's taskmasters set over them, were beaten, saying: Why did you not finish your quota to make bricks as before, both yesterday and today?
And the foremen of the sons of Yisroel came and cried out to Paroh, saying: Why do You do this to Your servants?
Straw is not given to Your servants, and they say to us: Make bricks, and behold, Your servants are beaten, and it is a sin against Your people.
And he said: You are lazy, lazy. Therefore you say: Let us go and sacrifice to Havayah.
And now, go work, and straw will not be given to you, and the count of bricks you shall deliver.
And the foremen of the sons of Yisroel saw themselves in distress, saying: Do not diminish from your bricks, each day's portion on its day.
And they encountered Moshe and Aharon, who were standing to meet them as they came out from before Paroh.
And they said to them: May Havayah look upon you and judge you, for you have made our reputation foul in the eyes of Paroh and in the eyes of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us.
And Moshe returned to Havayah, and he said: My Master, why have You harmed this people? Why did You send me?
For since I came to Paroh to speak in Your name, he has harmed this people, and You have not saved Your people.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Now you will see what I will do to Paroh, for with a strong hand he will send them, and with a strong hand he will drive them from his land.
And Elokim spoke to Moshe, and He said to him: I am Havayah.
And I appeared to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, as El Shaddai, and by My name Havayah I was not known to them.
And I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Kena'an, the land of their sojourning, in which they sojourned.
And I also have heard the groaning of the sons of Yisroel, whom the Mitzrim enslave, and I remembered My covenant.

Therefore, say to the sons of Yisroel: I am Havayah, and I will bring you out from under the burdens of Mitzrayim, and I will deliver you from their labor, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.
And I will take you to Me as a people, and I will be Elokim for you, and you will know that I am Havayah your Elokim, who brings you out from under the burdens of Mitzrayim.
And I will bring you to the land, concerning which I raised My hand to give it to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, and I will give it to you as a heritage: I am Havayah.
And Moshe spoke so to the sons of Yisroel, but they did not listen to Moshe, because of shortness of spirit and because of hard labor.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Come, speak to Paroh king of Mitzrayim, and he will send the sons of Yisroel from his land.
And Moshe spoke before Havayah, saying: Behold, the sons of Yisroel did not listen to me, and how will Paroh listen to me, and I am of obstructed lips?
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, and He commanded them concerning the sons of Yisroel, and concerning Paroh king of Mitzrayim, to bring out the sons of Yisroel from the land of Mitzrayim.
These are the heads of their fathers' houses: The sons of Reuven, the firstborn of Yisroel: Hanokh and Pallu, Chetzron and Karmi; these are the families of Reuven.
And the sons of Shimon: Yemuel and Yamin and Ohad and Yachin and Tzochar and Shaul, the son of the Kena'ani woman; these are the families of Shimon.
And these are the names of the sons of Levi by their generations: Gershon and Kehat and Merari, and the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven years.
The sons of Gershon: Livni and Shimi, by their families.
And the sons of Kehat: Amram and Yitzhar and Chevron and Uziel, and the years of the life of Kehat were one hundred and thirty-three years.
And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; these are the families of the Leviim by their generations.
And Amram took Yocheved his aunt as his wife, and she bore him Aharon and Moshe, and the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-seven years.
And the sons of Yitzhar: Korach and Nefeg and Zichri.
And the sons of Uziel: Mishael and Eltzafan and Sitri.
And Aharon took Elisheva, daughter of Aminadav, sister of Nahshon, as his wife, and she bore him Nadav and Avihu, Elazar and Itamar.
And the sons of Korach: Asir and Elkanah and Aviasaf; these are the families of the Korachites.
And Elazar son of Aharon took for himself from the daughters of Putiel as a wife, and she bore him Pinchas; these are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Leviim by their families.
This is Aharon and Moshe, to whom Havayah said: Bring out the sons of Yisroel from the land of Mitzrayim by their hosts.
They are the ones who speak to Paroh king of Mitzrayim, to bring out the sons of Yisroel from Mitzrayim: that is Moshe and Aharon.
And it was on the day Havayah spoke to Moshe in the land of Mitzrayim.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying: I am Havayah; speak to Paroh king of Mitzrayim all that I speak to you.
And Moshe said before Havayah: Behold, I am of obstructed lips, and how will Paroh listen to me?
And Havayah said to Moshe: See, I have made you as a mighty one to Paroh, and Aharon your brother will be your prophet.
You shall speak all that I command you, and Aharon your brother shall speak to Paroh, and he will send the sons of Yisroel from his land.
And I will harden the heart of Paroh, and I will multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh will not listen to you, and I will set My hand upon Mitzrayim, and I will bring out My hosts, My people, the sons of Yisroel, from the land of Mitzrayim with great judgments.
And the Mitzrim will know that I am Havayah, when I stretch out My hand over Mitzrayim, and I bring out the sons of Yisroel from their midst.
And Moshe and Aharon did as Havayah commanded them, so they did.
And Moshe was eighty years old, and Aharon was eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Paroh.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:
When Paroh speaks to you, saying: Give a wonder for yourselves, you shall say to Aharon: Take your staff and cast it before Paroh, it will become a serpent.
And Moshe and Aharon came to Paroh, and they did so as Havayah had commanded, and Aharon cast his staff before Paroh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
And Paroh also called the wise men and the sorcerers, and the magicians of Mitzrayim also did so with their secret arts.
And each man cast his staff, and they became serpents, and the staff of Aharon swallowed their staffs.
And the heart of Paroh hardened, and he did not listen to them, as Havayah had spoken.
And Havayah said to Moshe: The heart of Paroh is stubborn, he refuses to send the people.
Go to Paroh in the morning, behold, he goes out to the water, and you shall stand facing him on the bank of the Ye'or, and the staff that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand.
And you shall say to him: Havayah, Elokim of the Hebrews, sent me to you, saying: Send forth My people, and they will serve Me in the wilderness, and behold, you have not listened until now.
So Havayah says: By this you will know that I am Havayah: Behold, I strike with the staff that is in my hand upon the water that is in the Ye'or, and it will turn into blood.
And the fish that are in the Ye'or will die, and the Ye'or will stink, and Mitzrayim will be unable to drink water from the Ye'or.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Say to Aharon: Take your staff and stretch your hand over the waters of Mitzrayim, over their rivers, over their canals, and over their lakes, and over every gathering of their waters, and they will become blood, and there will be blood in all the land of Mitzrayim, in the wood and in the stones.

And Moshe and Aharon did so, as Havayah had commanded, and he raised the staff and struck the water that was in the Ye'or before the eyes of Paroh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the water that was in the Ye'or turned into blood.
And the fish that were in the Ye'or died, and the Ye'or stank, and the Mitzrim could not drink water from the Ye'or, and the blood was in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And the magicians of Mitzrayim did so with their secret arts, and the heart of Paroh hardened, and he did not listen to them, as Havayah had spoken.
And Paroh turned and came to his house, and he did not set his heart to this either.
And all of Mitzrayim dug around the Ye'or for water to drink, for they could not drink from the water of the Ye'or.
And seven days were completed after Havayah struck the Ye'or.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Go to Paroh, and you shall say to him: So Havayah says: Send forth My people, and they will serve Me.
And if you refuse to send them, behold, I will strike all your borders with frogs.

And the Ye'or will swarm with frogs, and they will come up and come into your house, and into your bedroom, and upon your bed, and into the house of your servants and your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading bowls.
And upon you, and upon your people, and upon all your servants, the frogs will come up.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Say to Aharon: Stretch out your hand with your staff over the rivers, over the canals, and over the lakes, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Mitzrayim.
And Aharon stretched his hand over the waters of Mitzrayim, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Mitzrayim.
And the magicians did so with their secret arts, and they brought up the frogs upon the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh called Moshe and Aharon, and he said: Plead with Havayah, and He will remove the frogs from me and from my people, and I will send the people, and they will sacrifice to Havayah.

And Moshe said to Paroh: Glorify yourself over me: For when shall I plead for you and for your servants and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses? Only in the Ye'or will they remain.
And he said: Tomorrow. And he said: As your word, so that you will know that there is none like Havayah our Elokim.
And the frogs will depart from you and from your houses, and from your servants and from your people; only in the Ye'or will they remain.
And Moshe and Aharon went out from before Paroh, and Moshe cried out to Havayah concerning the matter of the frogs that He had brought upon Paroh.
And Havayah did according to the word of Moshe, and the frogs died from the houses, from the courtyards, and from the fields.
And they gathered them into heaps, heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
And Paroh saw that there was relief, and he made his heart stubborn, and he did not listen to them, as Havayah had spoken.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Say to Aharon: Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the earth, and it will become lice in all the land of Mitzrayim.

And they did so, and Aharon stretched his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and the lice were upon man and upon beast; all the dust of the earth became lice in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And the magicians did so with their secret arts to bring out the lice, but they could not, and the lice were upon man and upon beast.
And the magicians said to Paroh: It is the finger of Elokim. And the heart of Paroh hardened, and he did not listen to them, as Havayah had spoken.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Rise early in the morning and stand before Paroh, behold, he goes out to the water, and you shall say to him: So Havayah says: Send forth My people, and they will serve Me.

For if you do not send forth My people, behold, I will send the swarm against you and against your servants and against your people and into your houses, and the houses of Mitzrayim will be filled with the swarm, and also the ground upon which they are.
And I will set apart on that day the land of Goshen, upon which My people stands, so that there will be no swarm there, so that you will know that I am Havayah in the midst of the land.
And I will set a division between My people and your people; tomorrow this sign will be.
And Havayah did so, and a heavy swarm came to the house of Paroh and to the house of his servants, and in all the land of Mitzrayim the land was ruined because of the swarm.
And Paroh called Moshe and Aharon, and he said: Go, sacrifice to your Elokim in the land.

And Moshe said: It is not right to do so, for the abomination of Mitzrayim we will sacrifice to Havayah our Elokim; behold, if we sacrifice the abomination of Mitzrayim before their eyes, will they not stone us?
A journey of three days we will go into the wilderness, and we will sacrifice to Havayah our Elokim, as He will say to us.
And Paroh said: I will send you, and you will sacrifice to Havayah your Elokim in the wilderness, only do not go very far; plead for me.

And Moshe said: Behold, I go out from before you, and I will plead with Havayah, and the swarm will depart from Paroh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow; only let Paroh not continue to deceive, by not sending the people to sacrifice to Havayah.
And Moshe went out from before Paroh, and he pleaded with Havayah.
And Havayah did according to the word of Moshe, and He removed the swarm from Paroh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained.
And Paroh made his heart stubborn this time also, and he did not send the people.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Go to Paroh, and you shall speak to him: So Havayah says, Elokim of the Hebrews: Send forth My people, and they will serve Me.
For if you refuse to send them, and you still hold them,
behold, the hand of Havayah is upon your livestock that is in the field, upon the horses, upon the donkeys, upon the camels, upon the cattle, and upon the flocks, a very severe pestilence.
And Havayah will distinguish between the livestock of Yisroel and the livestock of Mitzrayim, and nothing will die of all that belongs to the sons of Yisroel.
And Havayah set an appointed time, saying: Tomorrow, Havayah will do this thing in the land.
And Havayah did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Mitzrayim died, but of the livestock of the sons of Yisroel not one died.
And Paroh sent, and behold, of the livestock of Yisroel not one had died, and the heart of Paroh was stubborn, and he did not send the people.
And Havayah said to Moshe and to Aharon: Take for yourselves handfuls of soot of a furnace, and Moshe shall throw it toward the heavens before the eyes of Paroh.
And it will become dust over all the land of Mitzrayim, and it will become a rash erupting in blisters upon man and upon beast in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And they took furnace soot, and they stood before Paroh, and Moshe threw it toward the heavens, and it became a rash erupting in blisters upon man and upon beast.
And the magicians could not stand before Moshe because of the rash, for the rash was upon the magicians and upon all of Mitzrayim.
And Havayah hardened the heart of Paroh, and he did not listen to them, as Havayah had spoken to Moshe.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Rise early in the morning and stand before Paroh, and you shall say to him: So Havayah says, Elokim of the Hebrews: Send forth My people, and they will serve Me.
For this time I will send all My plagues to your heart, and to your servants, and to your people, so that you will know that there is none like Me in all the earth.
For now I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been wiped from the earth.
But for this I have kept you alive, in order to show you My power, and in order to declare My name in all the earth.
You still domineer over My people, not sending them forth.
Behold, at this time tomorrow I will rain a very heavy hail, which has not been like it in Mitzrayim since the day it was founded until now.

And now, send and gather your livestock and all that is yours in the field; every man and animal that is found in the field and is not gathered into the house, the hail will fall upon them and they will die.
He who feared the word of Havayah among the servants of Paroh drove his servants and his livestock into the houses.
And he who did not set his heart to the word of Havayah left his servants and his livestock in the field.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, and there will be hail in all the land of Mitzrayim, upon man and upon beast and upon all the greenery of the field in the land of Mitzrayim.
And Moshe stretched his staff toward the heavens, and Havayah gave thunder and hail, and fire went down to the earth, and Havayah rained hail upon the land of Mitzrayim.
And there was hail, and fire flashing in the midst of the hail, very heavy, which had not been like it in all the land of Mitzrayim since it became a nation.
And the hail struck in all the land of Mitzrayim all that was in the field, from man to beast, and the hail struck all the greenery of the field, and it broke every tree of the field.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Yisroel were, there was no hail.
And Paroh sent and called Moshe and Aharon, and he said to them: I have sinned this time; Havayah is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
Plead with Havayah, and there has been enough thunder of Elokim and hail, and I will send you, and you shall not continue to remain.
And Moshe said to him: When I go out of the city, I will spread my hands to Havayah; the thunder will cease, and the hail will be no more, so that you will know that the earth is Havayah's.
And as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear Havayah Elokim.
And the flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in ear and the flax was in stalk.
And the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they are late.
And Moshe went out from before Paroh, from the city, and he spread his hands to Havayah, and the thunder and the hail ceased, and rain did not pour upon the earth.
And Paroh saw that the rain and the hail and the thunder had ceased, and he continued to sin, and he made his heart stubborn, he and his servants.
And the heart of Paroh was hardened, and he did not send the sons of Yisroel, as Havayah had spoken through Moshe.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Come to Paroh, for I have made his heart stubborn, and the heart of his servants, so that I may place these signs of Mine in his midst.
And so that you may tell in the ears of your son and your son's son how I tormented Mitzrayim, and My signs that I placed among them, and you will know that I am Havayah.

And Moshe and Aharon came to Paroh, and they said to him: So Havayah says, Elokim of the Hebrews: Until when will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Send forth My people, and they will serve Me.
For if you refuse to send forth My people, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your border.

And they will cover the face of the earth, and one will not be able to see the earth, and they will eat the remnant of what was spared that remains for you from the hail, and they will eat every tree that grows for you from the field.

And they will fill your houses, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all of Mitzrayim, as your fathers and your fathers' fathers did not see from the day they were upon the earth until this day. And he turned and went out from before Paroh.
And the servants of Paroh said to him: Until when will this be a snare for us? Send the men, and they will serve Havayah their Elokim; do you not yet know that Mitzrayim is lost?
And Moshe and Aharon were returned to Paroh, and he said to them: Go, serve Havayah your Elokim. Who are the ones going?
And Moshe said: With our young and with our elders we will go, with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our cattle we will go, for it is a festival of Havayah for us.
And he said to them: So may Havayah be with you when I send you and your children; see that evil is before you.
Not so; let the men go now and serve Havayah, for that is what you seek. And he drove them out from before Paroh.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Stretch out your hand over the land of Mitzrayim for the locusts, and they will come up upon the land of Mitzrayim, and they will eat all the greenery of the land, all that the hail left.
And Moshe stretched his staff over the land of Mitzrayim, and Havayah brought an east wind in the land all that day and all the night; it was morning, and the east wind carried the locusts.
And the locusts came up upon all the land of Mitzrayim, and they settled in all the border of Mitzrayim, very severe; before them there were no locusts like them, and after them there will not be so.

And they covered the face of all the land, and the land was darkened, and they ate all the greenery of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail left, and no greenery remained on the tree or in the greenery of the field in all the land of Mitzrayim.
And Paroh hurried to call Moshe and Aharon, and he said: I have sinned against Havayah your Elokim and against you.
And now, please bear my sin just this time, and plead with Havayah your Elokim, and He will remove from me just this death.
And he went out from before Paroh, and he pleaded with Havayah.
And Havayah turned a very strong west wind, and it carried the locusts and cast them into the Yam Suf; not one locust remained in all the border of Mitzrayim.
And Havayah hardened the heart of Paroh, and he did not send the sons of Yisroel.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, and there will be darkness over the land of Mitzrayim, and the darkness will be felt.
And Moshe stretched his hand toward the heavens, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Mitzrayim for three days.
No man saw his brother, and no man rose from his place for three days, but all the sons of Yisroel had light in their dwellings.
And Paroh called Moshe, and he said: Go, serve Havayah; only your flocks and your cattle shall remain; your children also may go with you.
And Moshe said: You too will give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, and we will offer to Havayah our Elokim.
And our livestock will also go with us; not a hoof shall remain, for from it we will take to serve Havayah our Elokim, and we do not know with what we will serve Havayah until we come there.
And Havayah hardened the heart of Paroh, and he did not agree to send them.
And Paroh said to him: Go from me; beware for yourself, do not see my face again, for on the day you see my face you shall die.
And Moshe said: You have spoken rightly; I will not see your face again.
And Havayah said to Moshe: One more plague I will bring upon Paroh and upon Mitzrayim; afterward he will send you from here; when he sends you, he will drive you out completely from here.
Speak now in the ears of the people, and each man shall ask from his neighbor, and each woman from her neighbor, silver vessels and gold vessels.
And Havayah gave the people favor in the eyes of Mitzrayim; also the man Moshe was very great in the land of Mitzrayim, in the eyes of the servants of Paroh and in the eyes of the people.
And Moshe said: So Havayah says: About midnight I will go out in the midst of Mitzrayim.

And every firstborn in the land of Mitzrayim will die, from the firstborn of Paroh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the maidservant who is behind the mill, and every firstborn of the animals.
And there will be a great outcry in all the land of Mitzrayim, which has not been like it, and will not be like it again.
And for all the sons of Yisroel, a dog will not sharpen its tongue, against man or against beast, so that you will know that Havayah distinguishes between Mitzrayim and Yisroel.

And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow to me, saying: Go out, you and all the people who follow you, and afterward I will go out. And he went out from before Paroh in burning anger.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Paroh will not listen to you, so that My wonders will be multiplied in the land of Mitzrayim.
And Moshe and Aharon performed all these wonders before Paroh, and Havayah hardened the heart of Paroh, and he did not send the sons of Yisroel from his land.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe and to Aharon in the land of Mitzrayim, saying:
This month is for you the beginning of months; it is the first of the months of the year for you.
Speak to all the congregation of Yisroel, saying: On the tenth day of this month they shall take for themselves, each man, a lamb for a father's house, a lamb for the household.
And if the household is too few for a lamb, he and his neighbor who is near his house shall take according to the number of souls; each according to his eating you shall count for the lamb.
An unblemished lamb, a male a year old, shall be for you; from the sheep or from the goats you shall take it.
And it shall be for you for safekeeping until the fourteenth day of this month, and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yisroel shall slaughter it in the afternoon.
And they shall take from the blood, and they shall put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they will eat it.
And they shall eat the meat on that night, roasted over fire, and unleavened bread, with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
You shall not eat from it raw, nor cooked in water, only roasted over fire, its head with its legs and with its innards.
And you shall not leave from it until morning, and what remains of it until morning you shall burn with fire.
And so you shall eat it: Your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand, and you shall eat it in haste; it is a Pesach offering to Havayah.

And I will pass through the land of Mitzrayim on this night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Mitzrayim, from man to beast, and against all the powers of Mitzrayim I will execute judgments: I am Havayah.
And the blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you are, and I will see the blood and pass over you, and there will be no destroying plague upon you when I strike the land of Mitzrayim.
And this day shall be a remembrance for you, and you shall celebrate it as a festival to Havayah; for your generations you shall celebrate it as an eternal statute.

Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; but on the first day you shall remove leaven from your houses, for anyone who eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yisroel.

And on the first day there shall be a holy gathering, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy gathering for you; no work shall be done on them, except what is eaten for each person, that alone may be done for you.
And you shall guard the unleavened bread, for on this very day I brought your hosts out of the land of Mitzrayim, and you shall keep this day for your generations, an eternal statute.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.
For seven days leaven shall not be found in your houses, for anyone who eats leavening, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Yisroel, whether a stranger or a native of the land.
You shall not eat anything leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.
And Moshe called all the elders of Yisroel, and he said to them: Draw out and take for yourselves lambs for your families, and slaughter the Pesach offering.

And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and you shall touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood that is in the basin, and no man shall go out from the entrance of his house until morning.

And Havayah will pass to strike Mitzrayim, and He will see the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, and Havayah will pass over the entrance, and He will not let the destroyer come to your houses to strike.
And you shall keep this matter as a statute for you and for your children forever.
And it shall be, when you come to the land that Havayah will give you, as He spoke, you shall keep this service.
And it shall be, when your children say to you: What is this service to you?

And you shall say: It is the Pesach offering to Havayah, who passed over the houses of the sons of Yisroel in Mitzrayim when He struck Mitzrayim, and He saved our houses. And the people bowed and prostrated themselves.
And the sons of Yisroel went and did as Havayah had commanded Moshe and Aharon, so they did.

And it was at midnight, and Havayah struck every firstborn in the land of Mitzrayim, from the firstborn of Paroh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the captive who is in the dungeon, and every firstborn of the animals.
And Paroh rose in the night, he and all his servants and all of Mitzrayim, and there was a great outcry in Mitzrayim, for there was no house in which there was no dead.
And he called Moshe and Aharon in the night, and he said: Rise, go out from among my people, both you and the sons of Yisroel, and go serve Havayah as you have spoken.
Also your flocks and your cattle take, as you have spoken, and go, and bless me also.
And Mitzrayim pressed the people to hurry to send them from the land, for they said: We are all dying.
And the people carried their dough before it was leavened, their kneading bowls bound in their garments upon their shoulders.
And the sons of Yisroel did according to the word of Moshe, and they asked from Mitzrayim silver vessels and gold vessels and garments.
And Havayah gave the people favor in the eyes of Mitzrayim, and they granted their request, and they stripped Mitzrayim.
And the sons of Yisroel journeyed from Rameses to Sukkos, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides children.
And a mixed multitude also went up with them, and flocks and cattle, very great livestock.

And they baked the dough that they brought out of Mitzrayim into unleavened cakes, for it was not leavened, because they were driven out of Mitzrayim and they could not linger, and also they had not prepared provisions for themselves.
And the dwelling of the sons of Yisroel, which they dwelled in Mitzrayim, was four hundred and thirty years.
And it was at the end of four hundred and thirty years, and it was on that very day, all the hosts of Havayah went out from the land of Mitzrayim.
It is a night of watching for Havayah, to bring them out of the land of Mitzrayim; this is that night for Havayah, a watching for all the sons of Yisroel for their generations.
And Havayah said to Moshe and to Aharon: This is the statute of the Pesach offering: No foreigner shall eat from it.
And any man's slave, bought with silver, you shall circumcise him, then he shall eat from it.
A resident alien and a hired laborer shall not eat from it.
In one house it shall be eaten; you shall not take any of the meat from the house to the outside, and you shall not break a bone of it.
All the congregation of Yisroel shall do it.

And when a stranger lives with you and he would make the Pesach offering to Havayah, every male of his shall be circumcised, and then he shall come near to make it, and he shall be like a native of the land, but no uncircumcised person shall eat from it.
One law shall be for the native and for the stranger who lives among you.
And the sons of Yisroel did as Havayah had commanded Moshe and Aharon, so they did.
And it was on that very day, Havayah brought the sons of Yisroel out of the land of Mitzrayim by their hosts.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Sanctify to Me every firstborn, the firstborn of every womb among the sons of Yisroel, of man and of beast; it is Mine.

And Moshe said to the people: Remember this day, on which you came out of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage, for with a strong hand Havayah brought you out from here, and leavened bread shall not be eaten.
This day you are going out, in the month of Aviv.

And it shall be, when Havayah brings you to the land of the Kena'anim and the Chitim and the Emorim and the Chivim and the Yevusim, which He swore to your forefathers to give to you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall perform this service in this month.
Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day is a festival to Havayah.
Unleavened bread shall be eaten for the seven days, and leavened bread shall not be seen with you, nor shall leaven be seen with you, in all your border.
And you shall tell your son on that day, saying: It is because of this that Havayah did for me when I came out of Mitzrayim.
And it shall be a sign for you upon your hand, and a remembrance between your eyes, so that the teaching of Havayah will be in your mouth, for with a strong hand Havayah brought you out of Mitzrayim.
And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time, from year to year.
And it shall be, when Havayah brings you to the land of the Kena'anim, as He swore to you and to your forefathers, and He gives it to you,
you shall set apart to Havayah every firstborn of the womb, and every first offspring of an animal that you will have, the males are Havayah's.
And every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck, and every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying: What is this? You shall say to him: With strength of hand Havayah brought us out of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.

And it was, when Paroh refused to send us, Havayah killed every firstborn in the land of Mitzrayim, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast; therefore I sacrifice to Havayah every firstborn of the womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.
And it shall be a sign upon your hand, and an ornament between your eyes, for with a strong hand Havayah brought us out of Mitzrayim.

And it was, when Paroh sent the people, Elokim did not lead them by way of the land of the Pelishtim, though it was near, for Elokim said: Lest the people reconsider when they see war, and they return to Mitzrayim.
And Elokim led the people around by way of the wilderness of the Yam Suf, and the sons of Yisroel went up armed from the land of Mitzrayim.
And Moshe took the bones of Yosef with him, for he had made the sons of Yisroel swear, saying: Elokim will surely remember you, and you shall bring up my bones from here with you.
And they journeyed from Sukkos, and they encamped in Esam, at the edge of the wilderness.
And Havayah went before them by day in a cloud pillar, to guide them on the way, and by night in a fire pillar, to give them light, to go by day and by night.
The cloud pillar by day and the fire pillar by night did not depart from before the people.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the sons of Yisroel, and they shall return and encamp before Pi HaChiros, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Tzefon; opposite it you shall encamp by the sea.
And Paroh will say of the sons of Yisroel: They are lost in the land; the wilderness has closed in on them.
And I will harden the heart of Paroh, and he will pursue them, and I will be glorified through Paroh and through his whole army, and the Mitzrim will know that I am Havayah. And they did so.

And it was told to the king of Mitzrayim that the people had fled, and the heart of Paroh and his servants turned against the people, and they said: What is this that we have done, that we have sent Yisroel from serving us?
And he harnessed his chariot, and he took his people with him.
And he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Mitzrayim, and officers over all of them.
And Havayah hardened the heart of Paroh, king of Mitzrayim, and he pursued the sons of Yisroel, and the sons of Yisroel went out with a high hand.
And Mitzrayim pursued them, and overtook them encamped by the sea, all the horses and chariots of Paroh and his horsemen and his army, by Pi HaChiros, before Baal Tzefon.
And Paroh drew near, and the sons of Yisroel lifted their eyes, and behold, Mitzrayim was marching after them, and they were very afraid, and the sons of Yisroel cried out to Havayah.
And they said to Moshe: Is it because there are no graves in Mitzrayim that you took us to die in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, to bring us out of Mitzrayim?
Is this not the matter that we spoke to you in Mitzrayim, saying: Leave us alone, and we will serve Mitzrayim, for serving Mitzrayim is better for us than dying in the wilderness?
And Moshe said to the people: Do not fear; stand and see the salvation of Havayah that He will do for you today, for as you have seen Mitzrayim today, you shall not see them again forever.
Havayah will fight for you, and you shall be silent.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the sons of Yisroel, and they shall journey.
And you, lift your staff, and stretch your hand over the sea, and split it, and the sons of Yisroel shall come into the midst of the sea on dry land.

And as for Me, behold, I am hardening the heart of Mitzrayim, and they will come after them, and I will be glorified through Paroh and through his whole army, through his chariots and through his horsemen.
And Mitzrayim will know that I am Havayah, when I am glorified through Paroh, through his chariots, and through his horsemen.
And the messenger of Elokim, who went before the camp of Yisroel, moved and went behind them, and the cloud pillar moved from before them and stood behind them.
And it came between the camp of Mitzrayim and the camp of Yisroel, and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it lit the night, and one did not come near the other all the night.
And Moshe stretched his hand over the sea, and Havayah drove the sea with a strong east wind all the night, and He made the sea dry land, and the waters were split.
And the sons of Yisroel came into the midst of the sea on dry land, and the water was a wall for them on their right and on their left.
And Mitzrayim pursued and came after them into the midst of the sea, all the horses of Paroh, his chariots, and his horsemen.
And it was in the morning watch, and Havayah looked down upon the camp of Mitzrayim in the fire and cloud pillar, and He threw the camp of Mitzrayim into confusion.
And He removed the wheels of their chariots, and He made them drive with difficulty, and Mitzrayim said: Let me flee from before Yisroel, for Havayah fights for them against Mitzrayim.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Stretch your hand over the sea, and the water shall return upon Mitzrayim, upon its chariots and upon its horsemen.

And Moshe stretched his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength at the turning of the morning, and Mitzrayim was fleeing toward it, and Havayah shook Mitzrayim in the midst of the sea.
And the water returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, all the army of Paroh that came after them into the sea; not one of them remained.
And the sons of Yisroel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea, and the water was a wall for them on their right and on their left.
And Havayah saved Yisroel on that day from the hand of Mitzrayim, and Yisroel saw Mitzrayim dead on the shore of the sea.
And Yisroel saw the great hand that Havayah did against Mitzrayim, and the people feared Havayah, and they believed in Havayah and in Moshe His servant.
Then Moshe and the sons of Yisroel sang this song to Havayah, and they said, saying: I will sing to Havayah, for He is highly exalted; the horse and its rider He cast into the sea.
Havayah is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation; this is my Elokim, and I will glorify Him, the Elokim of my father, and I will exalt Him.
Havayah is a warrior; Havayah is His name.
The chariots of Paroh and his army He cast into the sea, and the choicest of his officers were drowned in the Yam Suf.
The depths covered them; they descended into the depths like a stone.
Your right hand, Havayah, is glorious in power; Your right hand, Havayah, shatters the enemy.
And in the greatness of Your majesty You overthrow those who rise against You; You send forth Your wrath, it consumes them like straw.
And with the blast of Your nostrils the waters were piled; the flowing waters stood like a mound; the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.
The enemy said: I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoils; my desire shall be sated upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand will dispossess them.
You blew with Your wind, the sea covered them; they sank like lead in the mighty waters.
Who is like You among the powers, Havayah? Who is like You, mighty in holiness, awesome in praise, performer of wonders?
You stretched out Your right hand; the earth swallowed them.
You guided with Your kindness this people You redeemed; You led them with Your strength to Your holy dwelling.
Nations heard, they trembled; dread gripped the inhabitants of Peleshet.
Then the chieftains of Edom were alarmed; trembling gripped the mighty ones of Moav; all the inhabitants of Kena'an melted.
Dread and fear shall fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm they shall be still as stone, until Your people passes, Havayah, until this people whom You have acquired passes.
You will bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, Havayah, the Sanctuary, my Master, that Your hands established.
Havayah shall reign forever and ever.

For the horses of Paroh came with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and Havayah returned the waters of the sea upon them, and the sons of Yisroel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea.
And Miriam the prophetess, sister of Aharon, took the drum in her hand, and all the women went out after her with drums and with dances.
And Miriam answered them: Sing to Havayah, for He is highly exalted; the horse and its rider He cast into the sea.
And Moshe led Yisroel from the Yam Suf, and they went out to the Shur wilderness, and they walked three days in the wilderness and did not find water.
And they came to Marah, and they could not drink the water of Marah, for it was bitter; therefore its name is called Marah.
And the people complained against Moshe, saying: What shall we drink?
And he cried out to Havayah, and Havayah showed him a tree, and he cast it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There He set for them a statute and a law, and there He tested them.

And He said: If you listen to the voice of Havayah your Elokim, and do what is right in His eyes, and listen to His commandments, and keep all His statutes, all the diseases that I placed upon Mitzrayim I will not place upon you, for I am Havayah your healer.
And they came to Eilim, and there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they encamped there by the water.

And they journeyed from Eilim, and the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel came to the Sin wilderness, which is between Eilim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month since their exodus from the land of Mitzrayim.
And the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel complained against Moshe and against Aharon in the wilderness.

And the sons of Yisroel said to them: If only we had died by the hand of Havayah in the land of Mitzrayim, when we sat by the pots of meat, when we ate bread to satiety, for you have brought us out to this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with famine.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Behold, I will rain bread for you from the heavens, and the people shall go out and gather each day's portion on its day, so that I may test them whether they will follow My teaching or not.
And it shall be on the sixth day, and they will prepare what they bring, and it will be double what they gather day by day.
And Moshe and Aharon said to all the sons of Yisroel: In the evening you will know that Havayah brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim.
And in the morning you will see the glory of Havayah, for He has heard your complaints against Havayah, and what are we, that you complain against us?

And Moshe said: When Havayah gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to satiety, when Havayah hears your complaints that you complain against Him, then what are we? Your complaints are not against us, but against Havayah.
And Moshe said to Aharon: Say to the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel: Come near before Havayah, for He has heard your complaints.
And it was, as Aharon spoke to the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel, they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of Havayah appeared in the cloud.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

I have heard the complaints of the sons of Yisroel. Speak to them, saying: In the afternoon you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be satisfied with bread, and you shall know that I am Havayah your Elokim.
And it was in the evening, and the quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
And the layer of dew rose, and behold, upon the surface of the wilderness was a fine, grainy thing, fine as frost upon the earth.
And the sons of Yisroel saw, and they said one to another: What is it? For they did not know what it was. And Moshe said to them: It is the bread that Havayah has given you to eat.

This is the matter that Havayah has commanded: Gather from it, each man according to his eating, an omer per person, according to the number of your people; each man shall take for whoever is in his tent.
And the sons of Yisroel did so, and they gathered, some more and some less.
And they measured it with an omer, and he who took more had no excess, and he who took less had no lack; each man according to his eating they gathered.
And Moshe said to them: No man shall leave from it until morning.
But they did not listen to Moshe, and some men left from it until morning, and it became infested with worms and stank, and Moshe was angry with them.
And they gathered it morning by morning, each man according to his eating, and the sun grew hot and it melted.
And it was on the sixth day, they gathered double bread, two omers for each one, and all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moshe.

And he said to them: This is what Havayah said: Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Shabbos to Havayah; what you would bake, bake, and what you would cook, cook, and all that remains, set aside for you for safekeeping until morning.
And they set it aside until morning, as Moshe had commanded, and it did not stink, and there was no worm in it.
And Moshe said: Eat it today, for today is a Shabbos to Havayah; today you will not find it in the field.
Six days you shall gather it, and on the seventh day, Shabbos, there will be none on it.
And it was on the seventh day, and some of the people went out to gather, and they did not find.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Until when will you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?
See that Havayah has given you the Shabbos; therefore He gives you on the sixth day bread for two days. Let each man remain in his place; no man shall leave his place on the seventh day.
And the people rested on the seventh day.
And the house of Yisroel called its name manna, and it was like white coriander seed, and its taste was like a cake with honey.

And Moshe said: This is the matter that Havayah has commanded: An omerful of it for safekeeping for your generations, so that they will see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim.
And Moshe said to Aharon: Take one jar, and put there an omerful of manna, and set it before Havayah for safekeeping for your generations.
As Havayah commanded Moshe, Aharon set it before the Testimony for safekeeping.
And the sons of Yisroel ate the manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Kena'an.
And the omer is a tenth of an ephah.

And the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel journeyed from the Sin wilderness, on their journeys, at the word of Havayah, and they encamped in Refidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.
And the people quarreled with Moshe, and they said: Give us water, and we will drink. And Moshe said to them: Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Havayah?
And the people thirsted there for water, and the people complained against Moshe, saying: Why did you bring us up from Mitzrayim, to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?
And Moshe cried out to Havayah, saying: What shall I do for this people? A little more and they will stone me.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Pass before the people, and take with you from the elders of Yisroel, and take your staff with which you struck the Ye'or in your hand, and go.

Behold, I stand before you there upon the rock at Chorev, and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink. And Moshe did so before the eyes of the elders of Yisroel.
And he called the name of the place Massah and Merivah, because of the quarrel of the sons of Yisroel, and because they tested Havayah, saying: Is Havayah among us, or not?
And Amalek came and fought with Yisroel in Refidim.
And Moshe said to Yehoshua: Choose men for us, and go out and fight with Amalek; tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill, and the staff of Elokim will be in my hand.
And Yehoshua did as Moshe said to him, to fight with Amalek, and Moshe and Aharon and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
And it was, when Moshe raised his hand, Yisroel prevailed, and when he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.

And the hands of Moshe were heavy, and they took a stone and placed it under him, and he sat upon it, and Aharon and Hur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other side, and his hands were steady until the setting of the sun.
And Yehoshua defeated Amalek and its people by the sword.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Write this as a remembrance in the book, and set it in the ears of Yehoshua, for I will surely wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens.
And Moshe built an altar, and he called its name: Havayah is my banner.
And he said: Because a hand is upon the throne of Havayah, the war of Havayah against Amalek is from generation to generation.
And Yisro, priest of Midyan, father-in-law of Moshe, heard all that Elokim had done for Moshe and for Yisroel His people, that Havayah had brought Yisroel out of Mitzrayim.
And Yisro, father-in-law of Moshe, took Tziporah, wife of Moshe, after she had been sent away.
And her two sons, of whom the name of the one was Gershom, for he said: A stranger I was in a foreign land.
And the name of the other was Eliezer, for the Elokim of my father was my help, and He delivered me from the sword of Paroh.
And Yisro, father-in-law of Moshe, came with his sons and his wife to Moshe, to the wilderness where he was encamped, at the mountain of Elokim.
And he said to Moshe: I, your father-in-law Yisro, am coming to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.
And Moshe went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed and kissed him, and each man asked the other how he fared, and they came into the tent.
And Moshe told his father-in-law all that Havayah had done to Paroh and to Mitzrayim for the sake of Yisroel, all the hardship that met them on the way, and how Havayah delivered them.
And Yisro rejoiced over all the good that Havayah had done for Yisroel, that He had delivered them from the hand of Mitzrayim.
And Yisro said: Blessed is Havayah, who delivered you from the hand of Mitzrayim and from the hand of Paroh, who delivered the people from under the hand of Mitzrayim.
Now I know that Havayah is greater than all the powers, for in the matter in which they schemed against them.
And Yisro, father-in-law of Moshe, took a burnt offering and feast offerings to Elokim, and Aharon came, and all the elders of Yisroel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moshe before Elokim.
And it was on the next day, and Moshe sat to judge the people, and the people stood over Moshe from the morning until the evening.

And the father-in-law of Moshe saw all that he was doing for the people, and he said: What is this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, and all the people stand over you from morning until evening?
And Moshe said to his father-in-law: Because the people come to me to seek Elokim.
When they have a matter, it comes to me, and I judge between a man and his fellow, and I make known the statutes of Elokim and His laws.
And the father-in-law of Moshe said to him: The thing that you are doing is not good.
You will surely wither, both you and this people that is with you, for the matter is too heavy for you; you cannot do it alone.
Now listen to my voice, I will advise you, and Elokim will be with you: You shall be for the people before Elokim, and you shall bring the matters to Elokim.
And you shall warn them of the statutes and the laws, and you shall make known to them the way in which they shall walk and the deeds that they shall do.

And you shall seek out from all the people capable men, Elokim-fearing men, men of truth, haters of ill-gotten gain, and you shall set them over them as leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.

And they shall judge the people at all times, and it shall be, every great matter they shall bring to you, and every small matter they shall judge themselves, and it will be light for you, and they will bear with you.
If you do this thing, and Elokim commands you, you will be able to endure, and also all this people will come to its place in peace.
And Moshe listened to the voice of his father-in-law, and he did all that he said.
And Moshe chose capable men from all of Yisroel, and he set them as heads over the people, leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.
And they judged the people at all times; the difficult matter they brought to Moshe, and every small matter they judged themselves.
And Moshe sent his father-in-law, and he went to his land.
In the third month from the exodus of the sons of Yisroel from the land of Mitzrayim, on this day they came to the Sinai wilderness.
And they journeyed from Refidim and came to the Sinai wilderness, and they encamped in the wilderness, and Yisroel encamped there before the mountain.
And Moshe went up to Elokim, and Havayah called him from the mountain, saying: So you shall say to the house of Yackov, and tell the sons of Yisroel:
You saw what I did to Mitzrayim, and I carried you on eagles' wings, and I brought you to Me.
And now, if you will surely listen to My voice and keep My covenant, you shall be a treasured possession for Me from among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine.
And you shall be for Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Yisroel.
And Moshe came and called the elders of the people, and he set before them all these words that Havayah had commanded him.
And all the people answered together and said: All that Havayah has spoken we will do. And Moshe returned the words of the people to Havayah.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Behold, I come to you in the thickness of the cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and they will also believe in you forever. And Moshe told the words of the people to Havayah.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow, and they shall wash their garments.
And they shall be ready for the third day, for on the third day Havayah will descend before the eyes of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
And you shall set bounds for the people around, saying: Beware of going up the mountain or touching its edge; anyone who touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
No hand shall touch him, for he shall surely be stoned or surely be shot; whether beast or man, it shall not live. When the shofar sounds long, they shall go up the mountain.
And Moshe went down from the mountain to the people, and he sanctified the people, and they washed their garments.
And he said to the people: Be ready for three days; do not come near a woman.

And it was on the third day, in the morning, and there were thunder and lightning and a thick cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of the shofar was very strong, and all the people in the camp trembled.
And Moshe brought the people out of the camp toward Elokim, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
And Mount Sinai was all smoke, because Havayah descended upon it in fire, and its smoke rose like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled greatly.
And the sound of the shofar grew stronger and stronger; Moshe would speak, and Elokim would answer him with a voice.
And Havayah descended upon Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and Havayah called Moshe to the top of the mountain, and Moshe went up.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Go down, warn the people, lest they break through to Havayah to see, and many of them fall.
And also the priests who approach Havayah shall sanctify themselves, lest Havayah break out against them.
And Moshe said to Havayah: The people cannot go up Mount Sinai, for You warned us, saying: Set bounds around the mountain and sanctify it.
And Havayah said to him: Go, go down, and you shall come up, and Aharon with you, but the priests and the people shall not break through to go up to Havayah, lest He break out against them.
And Moshe went down to the people, and he said to them.
And Elokim spoke all these words, saying:
I am Havayah your Elokim, who brought you out of the land of Mitzrayim, from the house of bondage.
You shall have no other powers before Me.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor any image of what is in the heavens above, or what is on the earth below, or what is in the water under the earth.

You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them, for I am Havayah your Elokim, a zealous Elokim, who visits the wrongdoing of the fathers upon the children, upon the third generation and upon the fourth generation, to those who hate Me.
And I show kindness to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
You shall not take the name of Havayah your Elokim in vain, for Havayah will not clear one who takes His name in vain.
Remember the Shabbos day, to keep it holy.
Six days you shall work and do all your labor.

And the seventh day is Shabbos for Havayah your Elokim; you shall not do any labor, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and your animal, and your stranger who is within your gates.
For in six days Havayah made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and He rested on the seventh day; therefore Havayah blessed the Shabbos day and sanctified it.
Honor your father and your mother, so that your days will be long upon the land that Havayah your Elokim gives you.
You shall not murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, or his male servant, or his female servant, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.
And all the people saw the thunder and the flames, and the sound of the shofar, and the mountain smoking, and the people saw and trembled, and they stood far off.
And they said to Moshe: You speak with us, and we will listen, and let Elokim not speak with us, lest we die.
And Moshe said to the people: Do not fear, for Elokim has come to test you, and so that His fear will be upon your faces, so that you will not sin.
And the people stood far off, and Moshe drew near to the thick cloud where Elokim was.
And Havayah said to Moshe: So you shall say to the sons of Yisroel: You saw that from the heavens I spoke with you.
You shall not make with Me silver figures, and gold figures you shall not make for yourselves.

An earthen altar you shall make for Me, and you shall slaughter upon it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen; in every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you.
And if you make Me a stone altar, you shall not build it of hewn stones, for you lifted your sword upon it and profaned it.
And you shall not go up by steps to My altar, so that your nakedness will not be uncovered upon it.
And these are the laws that you shall set before them.
If you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall work, and in the seventh year he shall go out free, without payment.
If he comes in alone, he shall go out alone; if he is married, his wife shall go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall go out alone.
And if the servant shall say: I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free.
And his master shall bring him to the judges, and he shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not go out as the male servants go out.
If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, to whom she was designated, he shall help her to be redeemed; he shall not have power to sell her to a foreign people, in his betrayal of her.
And if he designates her for his son, he shall treat her as is the practice of the daughters.
If he takes another wife for himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, or her conjugal rights.
And if he does not do these three for her, she shall go out free, without payment.
One who strikes a man and he dies shall surely be put to death.
But one who did not lie in wait, but Elokim brought it to his hand, I will set for you a place where he shall flee.
And if a man acts deliberately against his neighbor to kill him by cunning, you shall take him from My altar to die.
And one who strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
And one who kidnaps a man and sells him, or he is found in his possession, shall surely be put to death.
And one who curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
And if men quarrel, and one strikes the other with a stone or with a fist, and he does not die but falls into bed,
if he rises and walks outside on his staff, the one who struck him shall be cleared; he shall give only his loss of livelihood, and he shall provide healing.
And if a man strikes his male servant or his female servant with a staff, and he dies under his hand, he shall surely be avenged.
But if he survives a day or two days, he shall not be avenged, for he is his property.

And if men fight and strike a pregnant woman, and her children are lost, but there is no fatality, he shall surely be fined, as the husband of the woman shall set upon him, and he shall give as the judges decide.
But if there is a fatality, you shall give a life for a life.
an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,
a burn for a burn, a wound for a wound, a bruise for a bruise.
And if a man strikes the eye of his male servant or the eye of his female servant, and destroys it, he shall send him out free for his eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his male servant or the tooth of his female servant, he shall send him out free for his tooth.
And if an ox gores a man or a woman and he dies, the ox shall surely be stoned, and its meat shall not be eaten, and the owner of the ox is cleared.

And if the ox was wont to gore from yesterday and the day before, and it was testified to its owner, and he did not guard it, and it killed a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner too shall die.
If a ransom is set upon him, he shall give the ransom of his life, according to all that is set upon him.
Whether it gores a son or it gores a daughter, according to this law shall be done to him.
If the ox gores a male servant or a female servant, he shall give thirty silver shekels to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.
And if a man uncovers a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit shall pay; he shall repay silver to its owner, and the carcass shall be his.
And if a man's ox strikes his neighbor's ox, and it dies, they shall sell the living ox and divide its money, and the carcass they shall also divide.
