Or if it is known that it is an ox wont to gore from yesterday, and its owner did not guard it, he shall surely pay an ox for the ox, and the carcass shall be his.
If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and slaughters it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for the ox, and four sheep for the sheep.
If the thief is found breaking in, and he is struck and dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
If the sun has shone upon him, there is bloodguilt for him; he shall surely pay; if he has nothing, he shall be sold for his theft.
If the theft is found alive in his possession, whether an ox or a donkey or a sheep, he shall pay double.
If a man lets a field or a vineyard be grazed, and sends his animal, and it grazes in another's field, he shall pay the best of his field and the best of his vineyard.
If a fire goes out and catches thorns, and a pile of grain or standing grain or a field is consumed, the one who lit the fire shall surely pay.
If a man gives his neighbor silver or vessels to guard, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall pay double.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall be brought to the judges, to swear that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbor's property.

For every matter of wrongdoing, for an ox, for a donkey, for a sheep, for a garment, for any lost thing of which he shall say: This is it, the case of both of them shall come to the judges; whoever the judges condemn shall pay double to his neighbor.
If a man gives his neighbor a donkey or an ox or a sheep or any animal to guard, and it dies or is injured or is carried off, and there is no witness,
the oath of Havayah shall be between the two of them, that he did not lay his hand upon his neighbor's property, and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay.
And if it is stolen from him, he shall pay to its owner.
If it is torn by a wild beast, he shall bring it as proof; he shall not pay for the torn animal.
And if a man borrows from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall surely pay.
If its owner is with it, he shall not pay; if it is hired, it comes for its hire.
And if a man seduces a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a bride price for her to be a wife for him.
If her father refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh out silver according to the bride price of virgins.
A sorceress you shall not let live.
Anyone who lies with an animal shall surely be put to death.
One who sacrifices to other powers shall be destroyed, except to Havayah alone.
You shall not mistreat a stranger, and you shall not oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Mitzrayim.
You shall not afflict any widow or orphan.
If you afflict him, when he cries out to Me, I will surely hear his cry.
And My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword, and your wives will be widows, and your children orphans.
If you lend silver to My people, to the poor who is with you, you shall not be as a creditor to him; you shall not charge him interest.
If you take your neighbor's garment as a pledge, you shall return it to him by sunset.
For that alone is his covering, it is his garment for his skin; in what shall he lie? And it shall be, when he cries out to Me, I will hear, for I am gracious.
You shall not curse judges, and a prince among your people you shall not revile.
The first of your crops and your juices you shall not delay; the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
So you shall do with your cattle and with your flock; seven days it shall be with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
And you shall be holy people to Me, and meat torn by a beast in the field you shall not eat; you shall throw it to the dog.
You shall not take up a false report; do not join hands with the wicked to be a corrupt witness.
You shall not follow the many to do evil, and you shall not answer in a dispute to bend justice, by following after the many.
And you shall not favor a poor man in his dispute.
If you meet the ox of your enemy or his donkey straying, you shall surely return it to him.
If you see the donkey of your enemy crouching under its burden, and you would hold back from helping him, you shall surely help him with it.
You shall not bend the judgment of your poor in his dispute.
Keep far from a false matter, and the innocent and the righteous you shall not kill, for I will not clear the wicked.
And you shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the clear-sighted and twists the words of the righteous.
And you shall not oppress a stranger, for you know the heart of a stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Mitzrayim.
And six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

And in the seventh year you shall let it lie fallow and leave it, and the poor of your people shall eat, and what they leave the wild beast of the field shall eat; so you shall do with your vineyard and with your olive grove.
Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, so that your ox and your donkey will rest, and the son of your maidservant and the stranger will be refreshed.
And all that I have said to you, you shall keep, and the name of other powers you shall not mention; it shall not be heard from your mouth.
Three times in the year you shall keep a festival to Me.

The Festival of Unleavened Bread you shall keep; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in it you came out of Mitzrayim, and they shall not appear before Me empty-handed.
And the Festival of the Harvest, the first fruits of your work that you sow in the field, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather your work from the field.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Master, Havayah.
You shall not slaughter the blood of My offering with leavened bread, and the fat of My festival offering shall not remain overnight until morning.
The finest of the first fruits of your land you shall bring to the house of Havayah your Elokim; you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk.
Behold, I send a messenger before you, to guard you on the way, and to bring you to the place that I have prepared.
Beware of him and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he will not forgive your transgression, for My name is in him.
For if you surely listen to his voice and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and hostile to those who are hostile to you.
For My messenger will go before you and bring you to the Emorim and the Chitim and the Perizim and the Kena'anim and the Chivim and the Yevusim, and I will wipe them out.
You shall not bow down to their powers, and you shall not serve them, and you shall not do as they do; you shall surely tear them down and surely smash their monuments.
And you shall serve Havayah your Elokim, and He will bless your bread and your water, and I will take illness away from your midst.
There shall be no woman who miscarries or is barren in your land; I will fill the number of your days.
I will send My terror before you, and I will confound all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
And I will send the hornet before you, and it shall drive out the Chivim, the Kena'anim, and the Chitim from before you.
I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become desolate and the wild beast of the field multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you increase and inherit the land.

And I will set your border from the Yam Suf to the sea of the Pelishtim, and from the wilderness to the River, for I will give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out from before you.
You shall not make a covenant with them or with their powers.
They shall not dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me, for you will serve their powers, for it will be a snare for you.
And to Moshe He said: Come up to Havayah, you and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisroel, and bow down from afar.
And Moshe alone shall come near to Havayah, and they shall not come near, and the people shall not go up with him.
And Moshe came and told the people all the words of Havayah and all the laws, and all the people answered with one voice and said: All the words that Havayah has spoken we will do.
And Moshe wrote all the words of Havayah, and he rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Yisroel.
And he sent the young men of the sons of Yisroel, and they offered burnt offerings, and they slaughtered bull peace offerings to Havayah.
And Moshe took half the blood and placed it in basins, and half the blood he sprinkled upon the altar.
And he took the book of the covenant and read it in the ears of the people, and they said: All that Havayah has spoken we will do and we will listen.
And Moshe took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, and he said: Behold, the blood of the covenant that Havayah has made with you concerning all these words.
And Moshe and Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisroel went up.
And they saw the Elokim of Yisroel, and under His feet was like a sapphire-brick work, and like the very heavens in purity.
And against the nobles of the sons of Yisroel He did not stretch out His hand, and they beheld Elokim, and they ate and drank.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Come up to Me to the mountain, and be there, and I will give you the stone tablets and the teaching and the commandment that I have written, to teach them.
And Moshe rose, and Yehoshua his servant, and Moshe went up to the mountain of Elokim.
And to the elders he said: Wait here for us until we return to you, and behold, Aharon and Hur are with you; whoever has a matter shall come to them.
And Moshe went up to the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
And the glory of Havayah rested upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days, and He called Moshe on the seventh day from the midst of the cloud.
And the appearance of the glory of Havayah was like a devouring fire on the top of the mountain, in the eyes of the sons of Yisroel.
And Moshe entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up to the mountain, and Moshe was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
Speak to the sons of Yisroel, and they shall take for Me a gift; from every man whose heart moves him you shall take My gift.
And this is the gift that you shall take from them: gold, and silver, and copper.
And sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair.
And rams' hides dyed red, and tachash hides, and acacia wood.
Oil for lighting, spices for the anointing oil and for the spice incense.
Onyx stones, and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastplate.
And they shall make for Me a Sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.
According to all that I show you, the pattern of the Mishkan and the pattern of all its vessels, so you shall make it.
And they shall make an acacia-wood Ark: two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
And you shall plate it with pure gold, within and without you shall plate it, and you shall make upon it a gold rim all around.
And you shall cast for it four gold rings, and place them on its four corners, and two rings shall be on its one side, and two rings shall be on its second side.
And you shall make acacia-wood poles, and plate them with gold.
And you shall bring the poles into the rings on the sides of the Ark, to carry the Ark with them.
In the rings of the Ark the poles shall be; they shall not be removed from it.
And you shall place in the Ark the Testimony that I will give you.
And you shall make a pure gold cover: two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide.
And you shall make two gold cherubs; you shall make them of hammered work, at the two ends of the cover.
And make one cherub from this end, and one cherub from that end; from the cover you shall make the cherubs at its two ends.
And the cherubs shall spread wings upward, sheltering with their wings over the cover, and their faces one toward the other; toward the cover shall be the faces of the cherubs.
And you shall place the cover upon the Ark from above, and in the Ark you shall place the Testimony that I will give you.

And I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from upon the cover, from between the two cherubs that are upon the Ark of the Testimony, all that I will command you for the sons of Yisroel.
And you shall make an acacia-wood table: two cubits long, and a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
And you shall plate it with pure gold, and you shall make for it a gold rim all around.
And you shall make for it a handbreadth frame all around, and you shall make a gold rim for its frame all around.
And you shall make for it four gold rings, and you shall place the rings on the four corners that are on its four legs.
Close to the frame the rings shall be, as housings for the poles to carry the table.
And you shall make the acacia-wood poles, and plate them with gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
And you shall make its bowls and its spoons and its tubes and its supports, with which it shall be covered; of pure gold you shall make them.
And you shall place showbread upon the table before Me always.
And you shall make a pure gold Menorah; the Menorah shall be made of hammered work; its base and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers shall be from it.
And six branches shall come out of its sides: three branches of the Menorah from its one side, and three branches of the Menorah from its second side.
Three finely wrought cups on the one branch, a knob and a flower, and three finely wrought cups on the other branch, a knob and a flower; so for the six branches that come out of the Menorah.
And on the Menorah, four finely wrought cups, its knobs and its flowers.
And a knob under the two branches from it, and a knob under the two branches from it, and a knob under the two branches from it, for the six branches that come out of the Menorah.
Their knobs and their branches shall be from it; all of it hammered pure gold work.
And you shall make its lamps, seven, and he shall kindle its lamps, and it shall give light toward its front.
And its tongs and its pans shall be of pure gold.
Of a pure gold talent he shall make it, with all these vessels.
And see, and make them in their form, as you are shown on the mountain.
And you shall make the Mishkan of ten sheets of fine twisted linen, and sky-blue wool and purple and scarlet; with cherubs, a craftsman's work, you shall make them.
The length of the one sheet shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of the one sheet four cubits; one measure shall be for all the sheets.
Five sheets shall be joined one to another, and five sheets shall be joined one to another.
And you shall make sky-blue wool loops on the edge of the one sheet, at the end of the joining, and so you shall do on the edge of the outermost sheet in the second joining.
Fifty loops you shall make in the one sheet, and fifty loops you shall make at the end of the sheet that is in the second joining, the loops facing one to another.
And you shall make fifty gold hooks, and join the sheets one to another with the hooks, and the Mishkan shall be one.
And you shall make goats'-hair sheets as a tent over the Mishkan; eleven sheets you shall make.
The length of the one sheet shall be thirty cubits, and the width of the one sheet four cubits; one measure for the eleven sheets.
And you shall join five sheets alone, and six sheets alone, and you shall double the sixth sheet toward the front of the tent.
And you shall make fifty loops on the edge of the one sheet, at the end of the joining, and fifty loops on the edge of the sheet of the second joining.
And you shall make fifty bronze hooks, and you shall bring the hooks into the loops, and join the tent, and it shall be one.
And the overhang that remains of the sheets of the tent, half the sheet that remains, shall hang over the back of the Mishkan.
And the cubit on this side and the cubit on that side, of what remains of the length of the sheets of the tent, shall hang over the sides of the Mishkan, on this side and on that side, to cover it.
And you shall make a red-dyed rams'-hide cover for the tent, and a tachash-hide cover above.
And you shall make acacia-wood boards for the Mishkan, standing upright.
Ten cubits shall be the length of the board, and a cubit and a half shall be the width of the one board.
Two tenons for the one board, joined one to another; so you shall make for all the boards of the Mishkan.
And you shall make the boards for the Mishkan: twenty boards for the side to the south.
And forty silver sockets you shall make under the twenty boards: two sockets under the one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under the one board for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the Mishkan, for the north side, twenty boards.
And their forty silver sockets: two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the one board.
And for the side of the Mishkan to the west, you shall make six boards.
And two boards you shall make for the corners of the Mishkan at the sides.
And they shall be even below, and together they shall be whole at its top, at the one ring; so it shall be for the two of them; they shall be for the two corners.
And there shall be eight boards, and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets: two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the one board.
And you shall make acacia-wood bars: five for the boards of the one side of the Mishkan,
and five bars for the boards of the second side of the Mishkan, and five bars for the boards of the side of the Mishkan, for the side to the west.
And the middle bar, inside the boards, shall pass from end to end.
And you shall plate the boards with gold, and their rings you shall make of gold, as housings for the bars, and you shall plate the bars with gold.
And you shall set up the Mishkan according to its pattern, as you were shown on the mountain.
And you shall make a sky-blue wool, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen curtain, a craftsman's work, with cherubs you shall make it.
And you shall place it upon four acacia pillars plated with gold, their gold hooks, upon four silver sockets.
And you shall place the curtain under the hooks, and you shall bring there, behind the curtain, the Ark of the Testimony, and the curtain shall divide for you between the Holy and the Holy of Holies.
And you shall place the cover upon the Ark of the Testimony in the Holy of Holies.
And you shall place the table outside the curtain, and the Menorah opposite the table on the side of the Mishkan to the south, and the table you shall place on the north side.
And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tent of sky-blue wool and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, an embroiderer's work.
And you shall make for the screen five acacia pillars, and plate them with gold, their hooks shall be of gold, and you shall cast for them five bronze sockets.
And you shall make the acacia-wood altar, five cubits long and five cubits wide; the altar shall be square, and three cubits high.
And you shall make its horns on its four corners; its horns shall be from it, and you shall plate it with copper.
And you shall make its pots for its ashes, and its shovels, and its basins, and its forks, and its pans; all its vessels you shall make of copper.
And you shall make for it a grate, a copper-mesh work, and you shall make on the mesh four copper rings on its four corners.
And you shall place it under the ledge of the altar from below, and the mesh shall be up to the middle of the altar.
And you shall make poles for the altar, acacia-wood poles, and plate them with copper.
And its poles shall be brought into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Hollow, of planks, you shall make it; as He showed you on the mountain, so shall they make it.
And you shall make the courtyard of the Mishkan: for the side to the south, fine twisted linen hangings for the courtyard, one hundred cubits long for the one side.
And its twenty pillars, and their twenty copper sockets; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
And likewise for the north side, in length, hangings one hundred cubits long, its twenty pillars, and their twenty copper sockets; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
And for the width of the courtyard on the west side, fifty-cubit hangings, their ten pillars, and their ten sockets.
And the width of the courtyard on the east side, toward the sunrise, shall be fifty cubits.
And fifteen-cubit hangings for the one side, their three pillars, and their three sockets.
And for the second side, fifteen-cubit hangings, their three pillars, and their three sockets.
And for the gate of the courtyard, a twenty-cubit screen, of sky-blue wool and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, an embroiderer's work; their four pillars, and their four sockets.
All the pillars of the courtyard all around shall be banded with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their copper sockets.
The length of the courtyard shall be one hundred cubits, and the width fifty by fifty, and the height five cubits, of fine twisted linen, and their copper sockets.
All the vessels of the Mishkan, for all its service, and all its pegs, and all the pegs of the courtyard, shall be copper.
And you shall command the sons of Yisroel, and they shall bring to you pure olive oil, pressed, for the light, to kindle a lamp continually.

In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain that is before the Testimony, Aharon and his sons shall set it in order, from evening until morning before Havayah; it is an eternal statute for their generations, from the sons of Yisroel.
And you, bring near to you Aharon your brother, and his sons with him, from among the sons of Yisroel, to serve as priests to Me: Aharon, Nadav and Avihu, Elazar and Itamar, the sons of Aharon.
And you shall make holy garments for Aharon your brother, for glory and for splendor.
And you shall speak to all the wise-hearted, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and they shall make the garments of Aharon, to sanctify him, to serve as a priest to Me.

And these are the garments that they shall make: a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a quilted tunic, a mitre, and a sash; and they shall make holy garments for Aharon your brother and for his sons, to serve as priests to Me.
And they shall take the gold, and the sky-blue wool, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the linen.
And they shall make the gold, sky-blue wool, purple, scarlet, and fine twisted linen ephod, a craftsman's work.
It shall have two shoulder pieces joined to its two ends, and it shall be joined.
And the belt of his ephod, which is upon it, shall be of like craftsmanship, from it: gold, sky-blue wool and purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen.
And you shall take two onyx stones, and engrave upon them the names of the sons of Yisroel.
Six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the six that remain on the second stone, according to their birth.
Like an engraver's work in stone, like signet engravings, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Yisroel; you shall make them set in gold settings.

And you shall place the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, remembrance stones for the sons of Yisroel, and Aharon shall carry their names before Havayah on his two shoulders for a remembrance.
And you shall make gold settings.
And two pure gold chains, you shall make them of braided work, and you shall set the braided chains on the settings.
And you shall make a judgment breastplate, a craftsman's work; like the ephod's work you shall make it; of gold, sky-blue wool and purple and scarlet, and fine twisted linen you shall make it.
Square it shall be, doubled; a span long, and a span wide.
And you shall set in it a stone setting, four stone rows: an odem, pitdah, and barekes row; this is the first row.
And the second row: nofech, sapphire, and yahalom.
And the third row: leshem, shevo, and achlamah.
And the fourth row: tarshish, and shoham, and yashfeh; they shall be set in gold in their settings.
And the stones shall be according to the names of the sons of Yisroel, twelve, according to their names; like signet engravings, each according to its name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
And you shall make on the breastplate bordering pure gold braided chains.
And you shall make on the breastplate two gold rings, and you shall put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
And you shall put the two gold braids on the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
And the other two ends of the two braids you shall put on the two settings, and you shall place them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward its front.
And you shall make two gold rings, and you shall place them on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge, which is toward the ephod, on the inner side.
And you shall make two gold rings, and you shall put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, from below, toward its front, beside its seam, above the belt of the ephod.

And they shall lace the breastplate from its rings to the rings of the ephod with a sky-blue wool thread, to be on the belt of the ephod, and the breastplate shall not be loosened from upon the ephod.
And Aharon shall bear the names of the sons of Yisroel on the judgment breastplate upon his heart, when he enters the Holy, for a remembrance before Havayah continually.

And you shall place the Urim and the Tumim in the judgment breastplate, and they shall be upon the heart of Aharon when he enters before Havayah, and Aharon shall bear the judgment of the sons of Yisroel upon his heart before Havayah continually.
And you shall make the robe of the ephod entirely sky-blue wool.
And the opening for his head shall be within it; a hem, a weaver's work, shall be around its opening, like the opening of a coat of mail it shall be for it, so that it will not be torn.
And you shall make on its hem sky-blue wool, purple, and scarlet pomegranates, all around its hem, and gold bells among them all around.
A golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around.
And it shall be on Aharon to serve, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the Holy before Havayah, and when he goes out, and he will not die.
And you shall make a pure gold diadem, and engrave upon it, like signet engravings: Holy to Havayah.
And you shall place on it a sky-blue wool thread, and it shall be upon the mitre; toward the front of the mitre it shall be.

And it shall be on the forehead of Aharon, and Aharon shall bear the wrongdoing of the holy things that the sons of Yisroel shall sanctify, for all their holy gifts, and it shall be on his forehead always, for acceptance for them before Havayah.
And you shall quilt the linen tunic, and you shall make a linen mitre, and a sash you shall make, an embroiderer's work.
And for the sons of Aharon you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and caps you shall make for them, for glory and for splendor.
And you shall dress them, Aharon your brother and his sons with him, and you shall anoint them, and you shall invest them, and you shall sanctify them, and they shall serve as priests to Me.
And make for them linen trousers to cover the flesh of their nakedness; from the waist to the thighs they shall be.

And they shall be on Aharon and on his sons when they enter the Tent of Meeting, or when they approach the altar to serve in the Holy, so that they will not bear wrongdoing and die; it is an eternal statute for him and for his descendants after him.
And this is the thing that you shall do to them, to sanctify them to serve as priests to Me: Take one young bull, and two rams, unblemished.
And unleavened bread, and unleavened loaves mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil; of fine wheat flour you shall make them.
And you shall place them in one basket, and bring them near in the basket, with the bull and the two rams.
And you shall bring Aharon and his sons near to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and you shall wash them with water.
And you shall take the garments, and dress Aharon in the tunic and the robe of the ephod and the ephod and the breastplate, and gird him with the belt of the ephod.
And you shall place the mitre on his head, and you shall place the holy crown on the mitre.
And you shall take the anointing oil, and pour it on his head, and anoint him.
And his sons you shall bring near, and you shall dress them in tunics.
And you shall gird them with a sash, Aharon and his sons, and you shall bind caps on them, and the priesthood shall be theirs as an eternal statute, and you shall invest Aharon and his sons.
And you shall bring the bull before the Tent of Meeting, and Aharon and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.
And you shall slaughter the bull before Havayah, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And you shall take from the blood of the bull, and place it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you shall pour at the base of the altar.
And you shall take all the fat that covers the innards, and the lobe above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, and burn them on the altar.
And the flesh of the bull, and its hide, and its dung, you shall burn in fire outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
And you shall take the one ram, and Aharon and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
And you shall slaughter the ram, and you shall take its blood, and cast it around the altar.
And you shall cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its innards and its legs, and put them with its pieces and with its head.
And you shall burn the whole ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to Havayah, a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Havayah.
And you shall take the second ram, and Aharon and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

And you shall slaughter the ram, and take from its blood, and place it on the tip of the right ear of Aharon and on the tip of the right ear of his sons, and on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot, and you shall cast the blood around the altar.

And you shall take from the blood that is on the altar, and from the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aharon and on his garments, and on his sons and on the garments of his sons with him, and he shall be sanctified, and his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.

And you shall take from the ram the fat and the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards, and the lobe above the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, and the right thigh, for it is a consecration ram.
And one cake of bread, and one loaf of oil bread, and one wafer, from the basket of unleavened bread that is before Havayah.
And you shall place everything on the palms of Aharon and on the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before Havayah.
And you shall take them from their hands, and burn them on the altar with the burnt offering, for a pleasing aroma before Havayah; it is a fire offering to Havayah.
And you shall take the breast from the investiture ram that is Aharon's, and wave it as a wave offering before Havayah, and it shall be a portion for you.
And you shall sanctify the wave-offering breast and the gift-offering thigh, which was waved and which was lifted, from the investiture ram, from that of Aharon and from that of his sons.

And it shall be for Aharon and for his sons as an eternal portion from the sons of Yisroel, for it is a gift, and it shall be a gift from the sons of Yisroel, from their peace offerings, their gift to Havayah.
And the holy garments of Aharon shall be for his sons after him, to anoint them with them and to invest them with them.
Seven days shall the priest from his sons who serves in his stead wear them, who comes into the Tent of Meeting to serve in the Holy.
And you shall take the investiture ram, and cook its meat in a holy place.
And Aharon and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And they shall eat them, with which atonement was made, to invest them and to sanctify them, and a stranger shall not eat, for they are holy.
And if anything remains from the meat of the investiture or from the bread until the morning, you shall burn the leftover in fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.
And you shall do so to Aharon and to his sons, according to all that I commanded you; seven days you shall invest them.
And a sin-offering bull you shall offer each day for atonement, and you shall cleanse the altar by atoning for it, and you shall anoint it to sanctify it.
Seven days you shall atone for the altar and sanctify it, and the altar shall be most holy; anything that touches the altar shall be holy.
And this is what you shall offer upon the altar: two lambs a year old, for each day continually.
The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon.
And one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of pressed oil, and a libation of one-fourth of a hin of wine, for the one lamb.
And the second lamb you shall offer in the afternoon, like the morning meal offering and like its libation you shall offer it, for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Havayah.
A continual burnt offering for your generations, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before Havayah, where I will meet with you, to speak to you there.
And I will meet there with the sons of Yisroel, and it shall be sanctified by My glory.
And I will sanctify the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and Aharon and his sons I will sanctify, to serve as priests to Me.
And I will dwell among the sons of Yisroel, and I will be their Elokim.
And they will know that I am Havayah their Elokim, who brought them out from the land of Mitzrayim, to dwell among them; I am Havayah their Elokim.
And you shall make an altar for burning incense; of acacia wood you shall make it.
A cubit long, and a cubit wide; square it shall be, and two cubits high; from it shall be its horns.
And you shall plate it with pure gold, its top and its sides all around, and its horns, and you shall make for it a gold rim all around.
And two gold rings you shall make for it under its rim, on its two corners you shall make them, on its two sides, and they shall be housings for poles to carry it with.
And you shall make the acacia-wood poles, and plate them with gold.
And you shall place it before the curtain that is upon the Ark of the Testimony, before the cover that is over the Testimony, where I will meet with you.
And Aharon shall burn upon it spice incense; every morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
And when Aharon kindles the lamps in the afternoon, he shall burn it, a daily incense before Havayah for your generations.
You shall not offer upon it strange incense, nor a burnt offering, nor a meal offering, and a libation you shall not pour upon it.
And Aharon shall atone upon its horns once in the year, with the blood of the atonement sin offering; once in the year he shall atone for it for your generations; it is most holy to Havayah.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:

When you take the census of the sons of Yisroel, according to their count, each man shall give a ransom for himself to Havayah when they are counted, and there will be no plague among them when they are counted.
This is what everyone who passes among the counted shall give: half a shekel, by the holy shekel, twenty gera is the shekel; half a shekel as a gift to Havayah.
Everyone who passes among the counted, from twenty years old and above, shall give the gift of Havayah.
The rich shall not add, and the poor shall not subtract, from the half shekel, to give the gift of Havayah, to atone for your souls.

And you shall take the atonement silver from the sons of Yisroel, and give it for the service of the Tent of Meeting, and it shall be for the sons of Yisroel as a remembrance before Havayah, to atone for your souls.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
And you shall make a copper basin, and its base of copper, for washing, and you shall place it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you shall put water there.
And Aharon and his sons shall wash from it their hands and their feet.
When they enter the Tent of Meeting, they shall wash with water, and they will not die, or when they approach the altar to serve, to burn a fire offering to Havayah.
And they shall wash their hands and their feet, and they will not die, and it shall be for them an eternal statute, for him and for his descendants, for their generations.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
And you, take for yourself choice spices: pure myrrh, five hundred, and fragrant cinnamon, half of it, two hundred and fifty, and fragrant cane, two hundred and fifty.
And cassia, five hundred, by the holy shekel, and olive oil, a hin.
And you shall make it a holy anointing oil, a blend, a blender's work; a holy anointing oil it shall be.
And you shall anoint with it the Tent of Meeting, and the Ark of the Testimony.
And the table and all its vessels, and the Menorah and its vessels, and the incense altar.
And the burnt-offering altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base.
And you shall sanctify them, and they shall be most holy; anything that touches them shall be holy.
And Aharon and his sons you shall anoint, and sanctify them to serve as priests to Me.
And to the sons of Yisroel you shall speak, saying: This shall be holy anointing oil for Me, for your generations.
Upon the flesh of man it shall not be poured, and like it you shall not make according to its formula; it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
A man who blends like it, or who puts from it upon a stranger, shall be cut off from his people.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Take for yourself spices: stacte, and onycha, and galbanum, spices, and pure frankincense; each part shall be equal.
And you shall make it incense, a blend, a blender's work, well mixed, pure, holy.
And you shall grind some of it finely, and put some of it before the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you; it shall be most holy for you.
And the incense that you shall make, you shall not make for yourselves according to its formula; it shall be holy for you to Havayah.
A man who makes like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his people.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
See, I have called by name Betzalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Yehudah.
And I have filled him with a spirit of Elokim, with wisdom, and with understanding, and with knowledge, and with every kind of craftsmanship.
To devise designs, to work with gold, and with silver, and with copper.
And in cutting stones for setting, and in carving wood, to perform every kind of craftsmanship.
And I, behold, I have given with him Oholiav, son of Achisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and in the hearts of all the wise-hearted I have put wisdom, and they shall make all that I have commanded you.
The Tent of Meeting, and the Ark of the Testimony, and the cover that is upon it, and all the vessels of the Tent.
And the table and its vessels, and the pure Menorah and all its vessels, and the incense altar.
And the burnt-offering altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base.
And the woven cloths, and the holy garments for Aharon the priest, and the garments of his sons, to serve as priests.
And the anointing oil, and the spice incense for the Holy; according to all that I commanded you, they shall do.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
And you, speak to the sons of Yisroel, saying: My Shabbos days you shall surely keep, for it is a sign between Me and you for your generations, to know that I am Havayah, your Sanctifier.
And you shall keep the Shabbos, for it is holy for you; its profaners shall surely be put to death, for anyone who does work on it, that soul shall be cut off from among its people.
Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day is a Shabbos of rest, holy to Havayah; anyone who does work on the Shabbos day shall surely be put to death.
And the sons of Yisroel shall keep the Shabbos, to observe the Shabbos for their generations, an eternal covenant.
Between Me and the sons of Yisroel it is a sign forever, for in six days Havayah made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.
And He gave to Moshe, when He finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two Tablets of Testimony, stone tablets, written with the finger of Elokim.

And the people saw that Moshe delayed to come down from the mountain, and the people assembled against Aharon, and they said to him: Rise, make for us powers that will go before us, for this man Moshe, who brought us up from the land of Mitzrayim, we do not know what became of him.
And Aharon said to them: Remove the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.
And all the people removed the gold rings that were in their ears, and brought them to Aharon.
And he took from their hands, and fashioned it with a graving tool, and made it a cast calf; and they said: This is your power, Yisroel, who brought you up from the land of Mitzrayim.
And Aharon saw, and built an altar before it, and Aharon proclaimed and said: A festival for Havayah tomorrow.
And they arose early on the next day, and offered up burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings, and the people sat to eat and to drink, and they rose to frolic.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe: Go, descend, for your people, whom you brought up from the land of Mitzrayim, have acted corruptly.

They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them; they made for themselves a cast calf, and they bowed down to it, and slaughtered to it, and said: This is your power, Yisroel, who brought you up from the land of Mitzrayim.
And Havayah said to Moshe: I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
And now, let Me be, and My anger will burn against them, and I will destroy them, and I will make you into a great nation.
And Moshe pleaded before Havayah his Elokim, and said: Havayah, why shall Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Mitzrayim with great power and with a mighty hand?

Why shall the Mitzrim say, saying: For evil He took them out, to kill them in the mountains, and to destroy them from upon the face of the earth? Relent from Your burning anger, and reconsider the evil against Your people.

Remember Avraham, Yitzchak, and Yisroel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself, and You spoke to them: I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I said I will give to your descendants, and they shall inherit it forever.
And Havayah reconsidered the evil that He had spoken of doing to His people.
And Moshe turned and came down from the mountain, and the two Tablets of Testimony were in his hand, tablets written on both their sides; from this side and from that side they were written.
And the tablets were the work of Elokim, and the writing was the writing of Elokim, engraved on the tablets.
And Yehoshua heard the sound of the people in its uproar, and he said to Moshe: There is the sound of battle in the camp.
And he said: It is not the sound of a cry of triumph, and not the sound of a cry of defeat; the sound of a cry I hear.
And it was, when he came near to the camp, and he saw the calf and the dancing, that Moshe's anger burned, and he cast the tablets from his hands, and shattered them beneath the mountain.
And he took the calf that they had made, and burned it in the fire, and ground it until it was fine, and scattered it on the surface of the water, and gave the sons of Yisroel to drink.
And Moshe said to Aharon: What did this people do to you, that you brought a great sin upon them?
And Aharon said: Let the anger of my master not burn; you know the people, that it is in evil.
And they said to me: Make for us powers that will go before us, for this man Moshe, who brought us up from the land of Mitzrayim, we do not know what became of him.
And I said to them: Who has gold? Remove it. And they gave to me, and I cast it into the fire, and this calf came out.
And Moshe saw the people, that it was unsettled, for Aharon had left it unsettled, to shame before those who rise up against them.
And Moshe stood at the gate of the camp, and said: Whoever is for Havayah, to me! And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

And he said to them: So Havayah said, Elokim of Yisroel: Each man place his sword upon his thigh; pass back and forth from gate to gate in the camp, and slay each man his brother, and each man his neighbor, and each man his relative.
And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moshe, and there fell from the people on that day about three thousand men.
And Moshe said: Dedicate yourselves today to Havayah, for each man is against his son and against his brother, and to bestow upon you a blessing this day.
And it was on the next day, and Moshe said to the people: You have sinned a great sin, and now I will ascend to Havayah; perhaps I will atone for your sin.
And Moshe returned to Havayah, and said: Please, this people has sinned a great sin, and they made for themselves a gold power.
And now, if You will bear their sin — and if not, erase me, please, from Your book that You have written.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Whoever sinned against Me, I shall erase him from My book.
And now, go, lead the people to where I have spoken to you; behold, My angel will go before you, and on the day of My reckoning I will reckon their sin upon them.
And Havayah afflicted the people, because they made the calf that Aharon had made.

And Havayah spoke to Moshe: Go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up from the land of Mitzrayim, to the land about which I swore to Avraham, to Yitzchak, and to Yackov, saying: To your offspring I will give it.
And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Kena'ani, and the Emori, and the Chiti, and the Perizi, and the Chivi, and the Yevusi.
To a land flowing with milk and honey, for I will not go up in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I destroy you on the way.
And the people heard this evil word, and they mourned, and no man placed his ornament upon himself.

And Havayah said to Moshe: Say to the sons of Yisroel: You are a stiff-necked people; if for one moment I go up in your midst, I will destroy you. Now, remove your ornament from upon you, and I will know what I will do to you.
And the sons of Yisroel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Chorev.

And Moshe would take the tent, and pitch it outside the camp, far from the camp, and he called it the Tent of Meeting; anyone who sought Havayah would go out to the Tent of Meeting, which is outside the camp.
And it was, when Moshe went out to the tent, all the people would rise, and each man would stand at the entrance of his tent, and they would gaze after Moshe until he came into the tent.
And it was, when Moshe came into the tent, the cloud pillar would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and He would speak with Moshe.
And all the people would see the cloud pillar standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and bow down, each man at the entrance of his tent.
And Havayah would speak to Moshe face to face, as a man speaks to his neighbor, and he would return to the camp, and his servant Yehoshua, son of Nun, a lad, would not depart from within the tent.

And Moshe said to Havayah: See, You say to me: Bring up this people, and You have not let me know whom You will send with me, and You said: I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My eyes.
And now, if I have found favor in Your eyes, let me know, please, Your ways, and I will know You, so that I will find favor in Your eyes, and see that this nation is Your people.
And He said: My presence will go, and I will give you rest.
And he said to Him: If Your presence does not go, do not bring us up from here.

And how will it be known that I have found favor in Your eyes, I and Your people? Is it not by Your going with us, and we shall be distinct, I and Your people, from every people that is on the face of the earth?
And Havayah said to Moshe: This matter that you have spoken, I will do as well, for you have found favor in My eyes, and I know you by name.
And he said: Show me, please, Your glory.
And He said: I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of Havayah before you, and I will favor whom I will favor, and I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy.
And He said: You cannot see My face, for no man shall see Me and live.
And Havayah said: Behold, there is a place with Me, and you shall stand upon the rock.
And it shall be, when My glory passes, I will place you in the cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with My hand until I pass.
And I will remove My hand, and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets, which you shattered.
And be prepared for the morning, and you shall go up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and stand there for Me upon the top of the mountain.
And no man shall go up with you, and no man shall be seen on the whole mountain, and the flock and the herd shall not graze facing that mountain.
And Moshe carved two stone tablets like the first, and Moshe arose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, as Havayah had commanded him, and he took in his hand the two stone tablets.
And Havayah descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and He proclaimed the name of Havayah.
And Havayah passed before him and proclaimed: Havayah, Havayah, El, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in kindness and truth.

Keeping kindness for thousands, bearing wrongdoing and transgression and sin, and He will not clear the guilty; He visits the wrongdoing of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation.
And Moshe hastened and bowed to the ground and prostrated himself.
And he said: If I have found favor in Your eyes, my Master, let The Master go in our midst, for it is a stiff-necked people, and forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance.

And He said: Behold, I make a covenant; before all your people I will do wonders that have not been created in all the earth and in all the nations, and all the people in whose midst you are will see the work of Havayah, for it is awesome what I do with you.
Keep what I command you today; behold, I drive out from before you the Emori, and the Kena'ani, and the Chiti, and the Perizi, and the Chivi, and the Yevusi.
Beware lest you make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land into which you come, lest he be a snare in your midst.
For you shall smash their altars, and shatter their pillars, and cut down their sacred trees.
For you shall not bow down to another power, for Havayah, Whose name is Zealous, is a zealous El.
Lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they stray after their powers and slaughter to their powers, and they call you, and you eat of their slaughter.
And you take from their daughters for your sons, and their daughters stray after their powers, and they cause your sons to stray after their powers.
You shall not make molten powers for yourself.

You shall keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month of Aviv, for in the month of Aviv you came out of Mitzrayim.
Every firstborn of the womb is Mine, and every male of all your livestock, the firstborn of ox and sheep.

And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck, and every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem, and they shall not appear before Me empty-handed.
Six days you shall work, and on the seventh day you shall rest; in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
And you shall make the Festival of Weeks, the first fruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times in the year all your males shall appear before The Master, Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
For I will drive out nations from before you, and I will enlarge your border, and no man shall covet your land when you go up to appear before Havayah your Elokim three times in the year.
You shall not slaughter the blood of My offering with leavened bread, and the Pesach festival slaughter shall not remain until morning.
You shall bring the first of the first fruits of your land to the house of Havayah your Elokim. You shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk.
And Havayah said to Moshe: Write for yourself these words, for according to these words I have made a covenant with you and with Yisroel.
And he was there with Havayah forty days and forty nights; he did not eat bread, and he did not drink water, and He wrote upon the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Words.

And it was, when Moshe came down from Mount Sinai, and the two Tablets of the Testimony were in the hand of Moshe when he came down from the mountain, and Moshe did not know that the skin of his face was radiant because He had spoken with him.
And Aharon and all the sons of Yisroel saw Moshe, and behold, the skin of his face was radiant, and they feared to approach him.
And Moshe called them, and Aharon and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moshe spoke to them.
And afterward all the sons of Yisroel approached, and he commanded them all that Havayah had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
And Moshe finished speaking with them, and he placed a veil upon his face.
And when Moshe came before Havayah to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out, and he would come out and speak to the sons of Yisroel what he was commanded.
And the sons of Yisroel would see the face of Moshe, that the skin of Moshe's face was radiant, and Moshe would replace the veil upon his face until he came to speak with Him.
And Moshe assembled the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel, and said to them: These are the words that Havayah has commanded, to do them.
Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy day for you, a Shabbos of rest to Havayah; anyone who does work on it shall be put to death.
You shall not kindle fire in any of your dwellings on the Shabbos day.
And Moshe said to the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel, saying: This is the word that Havayah has commanded, saying:
Take from yourselves a gift to Havayah; everyone whose heart is generous shall bring it, the gift of Havayah: gold, and silver, and copper.
And sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair.
And rams' hides dyed red, and tachash hides, and acacia wood.
And oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the spice incense.
And onyx stones, and setting stones, for the ephod and for the breastplate.
And every wise-hearted man among you shall come and make all that Havayah has commanded.
The Mishkan, its tent, and its cover, its clasps, and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets.
The Ark, and its poles, the cover, and the screen curtain.
The table, and its poles, and all its vessels, and the bread of the Presence.
And the light Menorah, and its vessels, and its lamps, and the oil for the light.
And the incense altar, and its poles, and the anointing oil, and the spice incense, and the entrance screen of the Mishkan.
The burnt-offering altar, and its copper grate, its poles, and all its vessels, the basin and its base.
The hangings of the courtyard, its pillars, and its sockets, and the courtyard-gate screen.
The pegs of the Mishkan, and the pegs of the courtyard, and their cords.
The woven cloths to serve in the Holy, the holy garments for Aharon the priest, and the garments of his sons, to serve as priests.
And the whole congregation of the sons of Yisroel went out from before Moshe.

And every man whose heart stirred him came, and everyone whose spirit made him generous brought the gift of Havayah for the work of the Tent of Meeting, and for all its service, and for the holy garments.

And the men came with the women, everyone whose heart was generous brought a nose-ring, and an earring, and a ring, and a bracelet, every gold vessel, and every man who waved a gold wave offering to Havayah.
And every man with whom was found sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair, and rams' hides dyed red, and tachash hides, brought them.
Everyone who raised a gift of silver and copper brought the gift of Havayah, and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.
And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands, and they brought the spun yarn, the sky-blue wool, and the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.
And all the women whose hearts stirred them in wisdom spun the goats' hair.
And the leaders brought the onyx stones, and the setting stones, for the ephod and for the breastplate.
And the spice, and the oil, for the light, and for the anointing oil, and for the spice incense.
Every man and woman whose hearts made them generous to bring for all the work that Havayah had commanded to do by the hand of Moshe, the sons of Yisroel brought a freewill offering to Havayah.
And Moshe said to the sons of Yisroel: See, Havayah has called by name Betzalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Yehudah.
And He has filled him with a spirit of Elokim, with wisdom, and with understanding, and with knowledge, and with every kind of craftsmanship.
To devise designs, to work with gold, and with silver, and with copper.
And in cutting setting stones, and in carving wood, to perform every kind of craftsmanship.
And He has put in his heart to teach, he and Oholiav, son of Achisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with wisdom of heart, to do every engraver's work, and designer's work, and embroiderer's work in sky-blue wool, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in fine linen, and weaver's work, doers of every craft, and devisers of designs.

And Betzalel and Oholiav and every wise-hearted man, in whom Havayah had put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the Holy, did according to all that Havayah had commanded.
And Moshe called Betzalel and Oholiav and every wise-hearted man, in whose heart Havayah had put wisdom, everyone whose heart stirred him to approach the work to do it.
And they took from before Moshe all the gifts that the sons of Yisroel had brought for the work of the service of the Holy, to do it, and they brought to him further gifts morning by morning.
And all the wise men who did all the work of the Holy came, each man from his work that they were doing.
And they said to Moshe, saying: The people bring much more than enough for the work of the service that Havayah has commanded to do.
And Moshe commanded, and they proclaimed a voice in the camp, saying: Let no man or woman do more work for the gift of the Holy; and the people were held back from bringing.
And the work was enough for all the work to do it, and there was more than enough.
And all the wise-hearted among the doers of the work made the Mishkan, ten sheets of fine twisted linen, and sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubs, a craftsman's work, he made them.
The length of the one sheet was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of the one sheet was four cubits; one measure was for all the sheets.
And he joined five sheets one to another, and he joined five sheets one to another.
And he made sky-blue wool loops on the edge of the one sheet, at the end of the joining, and so he did on the edge of the outermost sheet in the second joining.
He made fifty loops in the one sheet, and he made fifty loops at the end of the sheet that was in the second joining; the loops faced one another.
And he made fifty gold hooks, and he joined the sheets one to another with the hooks, and the Mishkan was one.
And he made goats'-hair sheets as a tent over the Mishkan; he made eleven sheets.
The length of the one sheet was thirty cubits, and four cubits was the width of the one sheet; one measure was for the eleven sheets.
And he joined five sheets by themselves, and six sheets by themselves.
And he made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost sheet in the joining, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the sheet in the second joining.
And he made fifty bronze hooks to join the tent, to be one.
And he made a cover for the tent of red-dyed rams' hides, and a tachash-hide cover above.
And he made acacia-wood boards for the Mishkan, standing upright.
Ten cubits was the length of a board, and a cubit and a half was the width of each board.
Two tenons had one board, set parallel one to another; so he did for all the boards of the Mishkan.
And he made the boards for the Mishkan, twenty boards for the south side.
And he made forty silver sockets under the twenty boards: two sockets under the one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under the one board for its two tenons.
And for the second side of the Mishkan, for the north side, twenty boards.
And their forty silver sockets: two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the one board.
And for the back of the Mishkan, to the west, he made six boards.
And he made two boards for the corners of the Mishkan at the back.
And they were double below, and together they were complete at the top, to the one ring; so he did for both of them, for the two corners.
And there were eight boards, and their silver sockets, sixteen sockets, two sockets under the one board.
And he made acacia-wood bars, five for the boards of the one side of the Mishkan,
and five bars for the boards of the second side of the Mishkan, and five bars for the boards of the Mishkan for the west side.
And he made the middle bar to pass through the boards from end to end.
And he plated the boards with gold, and their rings he made of gold, housings for the bars, and he plated the bars with gold.
And he made the sky-blue wool, purple, scarlet, and fine linen curtain, a craftsman's work; with cherubs he made it.
And he made for it four acacia pillars, and he plated them with gold, their gold hooks, and he cast for them four silver sockets.
And he made an entrance screen for the Tent, of sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, an embroiderer's work.
And its five pillars and their hooks, and he plated their tops and their bands with gold, and their five sockets were copper.
And Betzalel made the acacia-wood Ark: two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high.
And he plated it with pure gold, within and without, and he made for it a gold rim all around.
And he cast for it four gold rings, on its four corners: two rings on its one side, and two rings on its second side.
And he made acacia-wood poles, and he plated them with gold.
And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the Ark, to carry the Ark.
And he made a pure gold cover: two and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide.
And he made two gold cherubs; he made them of hammered work, at the two ends of the cover.
One cherub from this end, and one cherub from that end; from the cover he made the cherubs at its two ends.
And the cherubs spread their wings upward, covering with their wings over the cover, and their faces were one to another; toward the cover were the faces of the cherubs.
And he made the acacia-wood table: two cubits long, and a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.
And he plated it with pure gold, and he made for it a gold rim all around.
And he made for it a handbreadth frame all around, and he made a gold rim for its frame all around.
And he cast for it four gold rings, and he put the rings on the four corners that were on its four legs.
The rings were opposite the frame, housings for the poles, to carry the table.
And he made the acacia-wood poles, and he plated them with gold, to carry the table.
And he made the vessels that were on the table: its dishes, and its spoons, and its bowls, and its pitchers, with which it would be covered; he made them of pure gold.
And he made the pure gold Menorah; he made the Menorah of hammered work; its base, and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers were from it.
And six branches came out of its sides: three branches of the Menorah from its one side, and three branches of the Menorah from its second side.
Three almond-shaped cups on the one branch, a knob and a flower, and three almond-shaped cups on the other branch, a knob and a flower; so for the six branches that came out of the Menorah.
And on the Menorah were four almond-shaped cups, its knobs and its flowers.
And a knob under two of the branches from it, and a knob under two of the branches from it, and a knob under two of the branches from it, for the six branches that came out of it.
Their knobs and their branches were from it, all of it one hammered piece of pure gold.
And he made its seven lamps, and its tongs, and its fire pans, of pure gold.
Of a pure gold talent he made it and all its vessels.
And he made the acacia-wood incense altar: a cubit long and a cubit wide, square, two cubits high, and its horns were from it.
And he plated it with pure gold: its top, its sides all around, and its horns, and he made for it a gold rim all around.
And he made two gold rings for it under its rim, on its two corners, on its two sides, as housings for poles with which to carry it.
And he made the acacia-wood poles, and he plated them with gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil, and the pure spice incense, a blender's work.
And he made the acacia-wood burnt-offering altar: five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high.
And he made its horns on its four corners; its horns were from it, and he plated it with copper.
And he made all the vessels of the altar: the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, and the forks, and the fire pans; all its vessels he made of copper.
And he made a grate for the altar, a copper-mesh work, under its ledge, from below, until its middle.
And he cast four rings on the four ends of the copper grate, as housings for the poles.
And he made the acacia-wood poles, and he plated them with copper.
And he put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with them; he made it hollow, of boards.
And he made the copper basin and its copper base, with the mirrors of the women who assembled at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
And he made the courtyard; on the south side, the hangings of the courtyard were fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits long.
Their twenty pillars, and their twenty copper sockets; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
And on the north side, one hundred cubits, their twenty pillars, and their twenty copper sockets; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
And on the west side, fifty-cubit hangings, their ten pillars, and their ten sockets; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver.
And on the east side, fifty cubits.
Fifteen-cubit hangings for the one side, their three pillars, and their three sockets.
And for the second side, from this side and from that side of the gate of the courtyard, fifteen-cubit hangings, their three pillars, and their three sockets.
All the hangings of the courtyard all around were fine twisted linen.

And the sockets for the pillars were copper, and the hooks of the pillars and their bands were silver, and the plating of their tops was silver, and all the pillars of the courtyard were banded with silver.

And the courtyard-gate screen was an embroiderer's work, of sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen; twenty cubits long, and five cubits high, corresponding to the hangings of the courtyard.
And their four pillars, and their four copper sockets; their hooks were silver, and the plating of their tops and their bands was silver.
And all the pegs of the Mishkan and of the courtyard all around were copper.
These are the reckonings of the Mishkan, the Mishkan of the Testimony, as they were reckoned by the word of Moshe, the service of the Leviim, by the hand of Itamar, son of Aharon the priest.
And Betzalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Yehudah, did all that Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And with him was Oholiav, son of Achisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman, and a designer, and an embroiderer in sky-blue wool, and in purple, and in scarlet, and in fine linen.
All the gold that was used for the work, for all the work of the Holy, the wave-offering gold, was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the holy shekel.
And the silver of those counted of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the holy shekel.
A beka per head, half a shekel by the holy shekel, for everyone who passed among the counted, from twenty years old and above, for six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
And the one hundred talents of silver were to cast the sockets of the Holy and the sockets of the curtain: one hundred sockets for the one hundred talents, a talent for a socket.
And of the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, and he plated their tops and banded them.
And the wave-offering copper was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
And he made with it the sockets of the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and the copper altar, and its copper grate, and all the vessels of the altar.
And the sockets of the courtyard all around, and the sockets of the gate of the courtyard, and all the pegs of the Mishkan, and all the pegs of the courtyard all around.
And of the sky-blue wool, and the purple, and the scarlet, they made the woven cloths to serve in the Holy, and they made the holy garments for Aharon, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he made the gold, sky-blue wool, purple, scarlet, and fine linen ephod.
And they hammered the gold sheets, and cut threads, to work within the sky-blue wool, and within the purple, and within the scarlet, and within the fine linen, a craftsman's work.
They made shoulder pieces for it, joined; at its two ends it was joined.
And the belt of his ephod that is upon it was from it, of like work: gold, sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And they made the onyx stones, set in gold settings, engraved with signet engravings, with the names of the sons of Yisroel.
And he placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, remembrance stones for the sons of Yisroel, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he made the breastplate, a craftsman's work, like the ephod's work: gold, sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.
It was square; they made the breastplate doubled; a span long and a span wide, doubled.
And they set in it four stone rows: an odem, pitdah, and barekes row, the first row.
And the second row: a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a diamond.
And the third row: a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
And the fourth row: a beryl, an onyx, and a chalcedony, set in gold settings in their mountings.
And the stones were according to the names of the sons of Yisroel, twelve, according to their names, signet engravings, each man according to his name, for the twelve tribes.
And they made on the breastplate bordering pure gold braided chains.
And they made two gold settings and two gold rings, and they put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
And they put the two gold braids on the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
And the two ends of the two braids they put on the two settings, and they put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward its front.
And they made two gold rings, and they put them on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge that was toward the ephod, on the inner side.
And they made two gold rings, and they put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, from below, toward its front, beside its seam, above the belt of the ephod.

And they tied the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a sky-blue wool thread, to be on the belt of the ephod, and the breastplate would not be loosened from the ephod, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he made the robe of the ephod, woven work, entirely sky-blue wool.
And the opening of the robe was within it, like the opening of a coat of mail, a hem around its opening, so that it would not be torn.
And they made on the hem of the robe sky-blue wool, purple, and scarlet pomegranates, spun together.
And they made pure gold bells, and they put the bells among the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around, among the pomegranates.
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe all around, to serve, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And they made the linen tunics, woven work, for Aharon and for his sons.
And the linen mitre, and the linen headdresses, and the linen trousers of fine twisted linen.
And the sash of fine twisted linen, and sky-blue wool, and purple, and scarlet, an embroiderer's work, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And they made the pure gold diadem of the holy crown, and they wrote upon it a writing, signet engravings: Holy to Havayah.
And they put upon it a sky-blue wool thread, to put it on the mitre from above, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And all the work of the Mishkan of the Tent of Meeting was finished, and the sons of Yisroel did according to all that Havayah had commanded Moshe; so they did.
And they brought the Mishkan to Moshe, the tent, and all its vessels, its clasps, and its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets.
And the red-dyed rams'-hide cover, and the tachash-hide cover, and the screen curtain.
The Ark of the Testimony, and its poles, and the cover.
The table, all its vessels, and the bread of the Presence.
The pure Menorah, its lamps, the lamps of the arrangement, and all its vessels, and the oil for the light.
And the gold altar, and the anointing oil, and the spice incense, and the tent-entrance screen.
The copper altar and its copper grate, its poles and all its vessels; the basin and its base.
The hangings of the courtyard, its pillars, and its sockets, and the courtyard-entrance screen, its cords, and its pegs, and all the vessels of the service of the Mishkan for the Tent of Meeting.
The woven cloths to serve in the Holy, the holy garments for Aharon the priest, and the garments of his sons, to serve as priests.
According to all that Havayah had commanded Moshe, so the sons of Yisroel did all the work.
And Moshe saw all the work, and behold, they had done it; as Havayah had commanded, so they had done, and Moshe blessed them.
And Havayah spoke to Moshe, saying:
On the first day of the first month you shall erect the Mishkan of the Tent of Meeting.
And you shall place there the Ark of the Testimony, and screen the Ark with the curtain.
And you shall bring the table, and arrange its setting, and you shall bring the Menorah, and kindle its lamps.
And you shall put the gold incense altar before the Ark of the Testimony, and you shall put the Mishkan-entrance screen.
And you shall put the burnt-offering altar before the entrance of the Mishkan of the Tent of Meeting.
And you shall put the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you shall put water there.
And you shall set up the courtyard all around, and you shall put the courtyard-gate screen.
And you shall take the anointing oil, and anoint the Mishkan and all that is in it, and sanctify it and all its vessels, and it shall be holy.
And you shall anoint the burnt-offering altar and all its vessels, and sanctify the altar, and the altar shall be most holy.
And you shall anoint the basin and its base, and sanctify it.
And you shall bring Aharon and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and wash them with water.
And you shall clothe Aharon with the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him, and he shall serve as a priest to Me.
And you shall bring his sons, and clothe them with tunics.
And you shall anoint them, as you anointed their father, and they shall serve as priests to Me, and their anointing shall be for them an eternal priesthood for their generations.
And Moshe did according to all that Havayah had commanded him; so he did.
And it was in the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, the Mishkan was erected.
And Moshe erected the Mishkan, and he set its sockets, and he placed its boards, and he put its bars, and he erected its pillars.
And he spread the tent over the Mishkan, and he put the tent cover over it from above, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he took the Testimony and put it into the Ark, and he placed the poles on the Ark, and he put the cover on the Ark from above.
And he brought the Ark into the Mishkan, and he placed the screen curtain, and he screened the Ark of the Testimony, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the north side of the Mishkan, outside the curtain.
And he arranged the bread arrangement upon it before Havayah, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he put the Menorah in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the Mishkan.
And he kindled the lamps before Havayah, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he placed the gold altar in the Tent of Meeting before the curtain.
And he burned upon it the spice incense, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he placed the Mishkan-entrance screen.
And he placed the burnt-offering altar at the entrance of the Mishkan of the Tent of Meeting, and he offered upon it the burnt offering and the meal offering, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he placed the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and he put water there for washing.
And Moshe and Aharon and his sons would wash their hands and their feet from it.
When they came into the Tent of Meeting, and when they approached the altar, they would wash, as Havayah had commanded Moshe.
And he erected the courtyard around the Mishkan and the altar, and he put the courtyard-gate screen, and Moshe finished the work.
And the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of Havayah filled the Mishkan.
And Moshe could not come into the Tent of Meeting, for the cloud rested upon it, and the glory of Havayah filled the Mishkan.
And when the cloud rose from over the Mishkan, the sons of Yisroel would journey on all their journeys.
And if the cloud did not rise, they would not journey until the day it rose.
For the cloud of Havayah was upon the Mishkan by day, and fire was in it by night, before the eyes of all the house of Yisroel, on all their journeys.
